articleTitle: Design and Performance Study of LCC-LCC and LCC-S Compensation Network for Wireless Charging of EV Battery
abstract: This work aims to study the compensation techniques used in wireless power transfer for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging application. Though there are several topologies for wireless power conversion Dual Active Bridge (DAB) configuration, better suits with wireless power transfer for its bidirectionality, high power density, ease of implementation and so on. Compensation network enhances the performance of the DAB in providing the constant current (CC) or constant voltage (CV) according to the battery charging status. This paper details the study on the performance of LCC-LCC topology and LCC- S topologies. The design values of magnetic elements of the compensation network are calculated analytically. The LCC-LCC and LCC- S compensations implementation in DAB converter is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. The results were obtained and compared with the symmetrical LCC and LCC- S compensation on the factors of efficiency, output power, transmitter current and receiver current.

articleTitle: A Multi-leg Powered Constant Voltage On-Road Charging System With an LCC-S Compensation
abstract: A Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC) system extends the travelling distance and lowers the Electric Vehicles heavy volume (EV) battery requirement. The High-frequency, High-Power inverter energizes the charging coupler embedded in the roadways. The EV batteries require a constant charging profile to extend their life. This paper suggests a constant voltage charging methodology for the DWC system with the LCC-S compensation network. A regression learning algorithm assists in determining the optimal value of the compensation network. The algorithm with a lower root means square value decides the optimal network value concerning the co-efficient of coupling. The five-leg inverter energizes the charging couplers, and the transmitter pads transfer the energy over 150 mm. The charging system delivers a nominal voltage of 350 V to the storage device. The overall efficiency of the proposed DWC system is 94.3% during constant voltage charging.

articleTitle: Effects of Realistic Driving Profiles on the Degradation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: This study explores the aging characteristics of lithium-ion batteries under conventional cycling tests and realistic driving profile tests. We employ regular capacity tests and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for a comprehensive analysis of state of health. For this investigation, we used commercial, round LiFePO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>cells in the 21700 format. The findings highlight more severe capacity loss under realistic driving profile tests compared to conventional cycling. This discrepancy hinting towards recuperation phases as a key factor in accelerated aging for lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles. This research underscores the importance of using realistic load scenarios for assessing battery life and may contribute to the development of more advanced battery management systems in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: A New Single Phase Dual Output Z-Source Inverter
abstract: In this article, a new single-phase dual output z-source inverter is introduced for electric drive applications to control the two outputs independently in terms of modulation index, frequency, phase, and load with optimal device count. Due to coupling with a z-source impedance network, the proposed configuration can boost the supply voltage to meet the load requirements. Moreover, the comparative analysis is done with existing dual output topologies to show the limits and merits of the proposed inverter such as the switch count, passive components, cost, efficiency, etc. On the other hand, the modified sinusoidal pulse width modulation technique is implemented to generate both shoot-through pulses for z-source operation and actual pulses for a dual output operation. Furthermore, the validation of the proposed work is verified in MATLAB /SIMULINK software followed by real-time simulation through the OPAL-RT platform.

articleTitle: Pragmatic Model-Based Design approach to accelerate and scale the EV Skills development
abstract: While this is an exciting time to be a part of the EV industry, there are many fundamental challenges that all ecosystem participants must address to effectively meet the demands of a rapidly growing market. In this paper we will focus on two of the challenges around the need for efficiency improvement and reduction in development cost and time. While there is a large pool of professionals trained in conventional automotive technologies, there is a pressing need to reskill and upskill the existing workforce and bring in system-level thinking as the industry moves from Conventional powertrain to Electrified powertrains. In order to achieve this, there's a need for the workforce to develop and expand their EV development skills in motor control, battery management, fuel cells, electrical systems, and system simulation. In this paper, a pragmatic model-based design approach has been proposed to accelerate and scale the EV Skills development through the systematic use of models and data. Pragmatic approach does not require starting from the ground up or completely overhauling existing processes and assets. Just the reverse; its fundamental principle is reuse: In pragmatic model-based design approach, data, and models—and the engineering teams’ associated skills in developing analytics, models, and simulations—are applied systematically to workflows throughout the life cycle of the product or service. The approach proposed in the paper focusses on establishing a framework for integration of process, people and tools that can help in accelerating the journey of EV makers from prototyping to production. We will also examine a case study from Mahindra on how workforce and leadership is transforming to enable the forthcoming electric vehicle revolution.

articleTitle: Lumped Parameter Thermal Model for IPMSM Motors Including Housing, Bearing and Endcap for Vehicle Applications
abstract: One of the constraints to motor performance is temperature limits of its components. Studying performance at the system level, requires motor thermal model to be fast running and accurate. The motor configuration under study is realized into a 26-node reduced order thermal network with parameterized resistances and capacitances which shall be simulated and verified for accuracy of temperature predictions. Conduction (radial and axial) and convection heat transfer are considered for calculations. Empirical correlations are proposed for heat transfer coefficients of various parts of machine utilizing geometrical and material parameters as input. Technical papers to date have discussed radial heat transfers for main motor components. This paper investigates the radial and axial heat transfers for all motor components including housing, endcap, end plate and bearing. This model can be integrated into system models for temperature predictions of critical components or for motor optimization purposes for different motor designs and cooling configurations.

articleTitle: Microstructural and Compositional analysis of Cyclic aged Lithium-Ion 18650 Cylindrical Cells Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) … Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP)
abstract: In recent years, lithium-ion batteries have become increasingly popular due to their high energy density and long cycle life. However, as these batteries undergo cyclic aging, they experience microcracks and electrode material loss due to physicochemical changes. These can significantly impact the performance and lifespan of the battery. Microcracks are small fractures that occur in the electrode material due to repeated expansion and contraction during charging and discharging cycles. These cracks can lead to a decrease in the battery's capacity and an increase in its internal resistance, ultimately resulting in reduced overall performance. Electrode material loss is another point that arises during cyclic aging. As the battery undergoes repeated charge-discharge cycles, some of the active materials on the electrodes may break down or dissolve into the electrolyte solution. This can lead to a decrease in capacity and an increase in internal resistance. It is crucial to understand and mitigate the causes of microcracking or material loss to create more stable and efficient lithium-ion batteries and to ensure the longevity and reliability of lithium-ion cells. The effects of such cyclic aging on 18650 cylindrical cells composed of Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC-811) and Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) were investigated in this study for fresh, 100, 300, and 500 cycles at room temperature with a constant C-rate of 1. The structural, morphological, and chemical changes were evaluated using Scanning Electron Microscopy, Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy and Elemental Mapping. The analysis showed that both cathode and anode electrode materials deteriorated significantly as cyclic ageing progressed.

articleTitle: Prediction of Sealant Performance Parameters using Kriging Model
abstract: O-rings are the essential sealants used in various engineering applications. In Fuel Cell, O-rings ensure proper functioning of various subsystems by preventing leakages of working fluid. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) of sealant assembly is performed for the virtual assessment. Performance of O-rings depend on multiple input parameters. Conventionally, an input parameter is varied to identify influence on performance parameters. This is inefficient and very extensive. This study proposes a novel methodology that predicts sealant performance and correlates inputs (design parameters) to outputs (performance parameters). In this method, Sequential Space Filling Sampling technique is used to generate design sample space with Design of Experiments (DOE) points. Preliminary design target verification is performed for all DOE points. FEA simulations are performed for the verified DOE points. Finally, statistical analysis is performed to develop Kriging and Machine Learning (ML) models for predictive modelling and selecting optimal design. ANOVA is performed to understand the influence of input design parameters on the output variables.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Feasibility Study of Electric Vehicle Battery Thermal Management System
abstract: Battery thermal management is a critical aspect in ensuring the efficient operation and longevity of energy storage systems. Excessive heat generation and poor thermal dissipation can adversely affect battery performance, safety, and overall lifespan. This study explores various methodologies for managing battery temperature to ensure the well-being of the battery and enhance its lifespan. To achieve effective thermal management, diverse techniques are employed, including forced air cooling, cooling plates, and liquid cooling. The proposed system aims to address the challenges associated with battery thermal management by leveraging the unique capabilities of TECs, it becomes possible to actively regulate the temperature and dissipate excess heat efficiently. In this study, an extensive examination was conducted on a 7S 3P battery pack (25<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}$</tex> 7.8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ah}$</tex>) to explore its thermal behavior when subjected to different dis(charging) rates. Transformer oil possesses excellent thermal conductivity, electrical insulation properties, and high flash point, making it a suitable choice for battery cooling applications. The investigation encompassed scenarios involving both natural convection and immersion cooling. By utilizing these approaches, the research sought to acquire comprehensive insights into the thermal dynamics of the battery pack and evaluate the performance of various battery cooling systems.

articleTitle: Improve Energy Efficiency of Hybrid Electric Tractor Drivetrain using Centralized Control
abstract: Most of the off-highway manufacturers are transitioning to sustainable solutions to reduce both emissions and energy consumption. A series of solutions are being deployed and investigated to transition to sustainable agriculture. Electrification is a proven technology to achieve energy efficiency which is already matured and getting popular. In case of, off highway equipment, electrification helps in delivering customer value under three major categories namely precision, productivity, and sustainability. Precision agriculture helps accurate application of products (seeds, fertilizer etc.) in the field, productivity guarantees the required system response with high performance controls whereas sustainability helps reduce the environmental impacts of our job and applied products. This paper establishes optimal supervisory control strategy on power split hybrid electric propulsion system of agriculture tractor to effectively manage and prioritize the required actuator performance while controlling the energy flow through and from power sources to consumers while meeting the vehicle-level precision, productivity, and sustainability objectives.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of Digitally Controlled Series Resonant Converter Using Software Frequency Response Analysis
abstract: Resonant converters are widely used topologies in applications demanding high gain, and high power density with higher efficiency due to their soft switching capabilities enabling higher switching frequency operations. Modeling techniques such as extended describing function-based method, dq based models are evolving in the literature to obtain plant and control transfer functions for resonant converters. In this paper, an attempt is made to obtain the model of a digitally controlled series resonant converter hardware prototype using the Software Frequency Response Analyzer (SFRA) tool considering wide line and load variations. Based on the obtained plant model, the controller is implemented in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> DSP, and the frequency response plots of the plant model, and compensated open loop gain obtained using the SFRA tool are presented for a 500 W digitally controlled Series Resonant Converter (SRC). The obtained plant model, and compensated loop gain from the hardware prototype are in good agreement with those obtained from the simulated switching converter model. The implemented compensator is effective in optimizing the dynamic performance of the converter and obtained closed-loop operation results are presented.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Motor and Battery Sizing and Scaling for EV Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of Motor and Battery Sizing and Scaling for electric vehicles (EVs) using the Dorleco SIM EV model. As EVs become increasingly popular, optimizing Motor, battery and cell sizes becomes crucial to enhance performance and maximize range. Three primary scaling methods, namely energy-based scaling, power-based scaling, and range-based scaling are evaluated in the context of the Dorleco SIM EV. The study considers various factors such as several parameters related to the vehicles' characteristics and performance are considered for evaluation. The analysis provides insights into their impact on real-world driving scenarios, vehicle performance, cost, and weight. The findings of this study using the Dorleco SIM EV model can serve as a valuable guide for researchers, engineers, and EV manufacturers in selecting appropriate sizing and scaling methods. By optimizing Motor, battery and cell sizing, EVs can achieve improved efficiency, extended range, reduced costs, and enhanced overall performance, contributing to the acceleration of sustainable transportation.

articleTitle: Life Estimation of Power Electronic Components in Electric Vehicle for Vibration Loads
abstract: Vibration plays a significant role in the performance and failure of a component or assembly. Severity of the vibration depends on several parameters including source of vibration and position of the component assembled in vehicle. Power electronic components (PEC) are the brain of electric vehicle (EV). Multiple power electronics are used in EV to perform various functions like to convert, control, and regulate the electrical energy. Due to its complexity in assembling small-size electronics with modules of large dimensions and huge mass, the effects of random vibrational loads transferred to PEC must be analyzed over a wide frequency range. The main intent of this study is to develop a robust Finite Element methodology to validate the PEC for fatigue failures due to road loads with better test correlation leading to shorter design cycle.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Power Transfer Efficiency in Wireless Charging of Electric Vehicles by Positioning System with Sensor-based Technology
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) system-based charging for an electric vehicle (EV) is becoming popular among EV industries and researchers because of its attractive features. However, the WPT technology has many problems in concern with power transfer efficiency (PTE). Mainly PTE is affected by lateral and angular misalignment. In this paper novel alignment strategy for addressing the misalignment issue between the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) coil. The proposed sensor-based positioning system aligns the Tx coil by tilting using stepper motor which is controlled by a controller based on the RF sensor signal output. Also, the coil systems were modelled and analysed theoretically using ANSYS-Maxwell simulation. The proposed positioning system is implemented and results were verified with developed proto type electric bike. Which transfer the power wirelessly and charges the 16Ah, 24V Li-ion battery at an efficiency of 93.4%

articleTitle: Optimal Transition of Fleets to Electric Vehicle using Mathematical Optimization
abstract: Due to sustainability push around the world, lot of depot operators are transitioning their vehicle fleet to electric vehicles. A depot often comprises of hundreds of diesel-powered vehicles, such as buses, trucks, last-mile delivery vans, etc. Before depot owners begin the move to sustainable transportation, there are many questions that need to be addressed. What kind of vehicle and charging infrastructure are needed. How to reduce the capital investment and daily operational cost. This paper proposes a methodology for optimal transition of fleet to electric vehicles. Dispatching and charging are the two sub-problems that make up the main issue. The method of mixed integer linear programming has been used to create two distinct algorithms. In order to maximize the use of electric vehicles, dispatch optimizes the vehicle to route mapping, which also optimizes the vehicle infrastructure. Its charge schedules are developed based on the vehicle route mapping and provided as input to the charging algorithm. Where power requirement is optimized for minimum depot peak power and charging cost, thus minimizing the charging infrastructure and daily operational cost.

articleTitle: An Electric Vehicles Based Virtual Inertia Control for Frequency Support of Low-Inertia Microgrid
abstract: The impetus to “Go Green” has led to the increasing integration of renewable energy into the emerging grid. The increased share of renewables in the existing grid results in decreased rotational inertia, which necessitates the requirement of fast and efficient inertia control techniques and energy storage devices. However, due to the high capital cost and running cost associated with energy storage devices, electric vehicles provide a promising solution for the emulation of inertia in the low inertia grid. The paper investigates the utilization of electric vehicles for enhancing the inertial emulation capacity and promoting frequency stability of the standalone microgrid. A Genetic Algorithm optimized derivative-type virtual inertia control that takes into account both inertia and damping in the virtual inertia loop along with electric vehicles has been proposed. The frequency response of the standalone microgrid under the proposed virtual inertia control utilizing electric vehicles has been investigated for different EV penetration levels, variations in loads, and uncertainty of the renewables. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control is validated by the comparative analysis of electric vehicles based virtual inertia control with the external energy storage devices based virtual inertia control with and without controller parameter optimization.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Torque Control for Enhanced SRM With Improving Drive Hardware Performance
abstract: Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) is the choice of next-generation electric vehicle (EVs) traction motor applications, due to their simple rotor structure, power and torque characteristics. However, this SRM drive suffers from high torque ripples, which may cause severe vibration and acoustics. Therefore, torque ripple is effectively reduced by control techniques. This paper proposes an enhanced model predictive torque control (MPTC) that minimizes torque ripple and improves system efficiency. The active voltage vector (VVs) selection is obtained by removing flux linkage, eight sectors in the SRM electric cycle, and minimum VVs at each control period. As a result, a single cost function designed with the weighting factor reduces torque ripple by selecting optimal VVs. The enhanced SRM dynamic motor model and proposed MPTC control are verified through simulation studies and experiments based on a four-phase 8/6 pole SRM drive system.

articleTitle: Ripple Test and Impedance Analysis Procedures for Normative Evaluation of HVDC Busses In Evs
abstract: This paper describes the importance of impedance analysis of individual, as well as connected components in a high voltage DC bus and best test practices to comply with normative standards. The HVDC bus is the “backbone” in any battery powered EV. It provides power transfer from battery to e-drives and supplies power to modules for heating/cooling, on-bord charging and other auxiliaries. However, voltage and current on the DC bus also comprise of AC components generated by inverters and other power consuming components. Voltage ripples may result in high current ripples on the DC bus, especially when ripple frequencies coincide with any modules’ low impedance resonance frequencies. These resonant current ripples can result in thermal destruction of power lines and modules, as well as in degradation of battery, e-motors and inverters alike. Consequently, such module and system ripple tests are required in OEM's and ISO test norms.

articleTitle: Analysis of Solvers in MATLAB for Power Converter Applications
abstract: A major concern of the existing transportation system is air pollution caused by the burning of fossil fuels. This problem can be minimized using battery electric vehicles (EVs) in which a battery is used as the main power source. The role of a DC-DC converter in modern-day EVs is highly significant in terms of fast charging and high efficiency. In this paper, a buck converter is modeled using volt- and amp-second balance equations and simulated using solvers, such as symbolic math toolbox (syms) and ordinary differential equations (ODE 45 and 23s). The accuracy of the solvers is calculated and the average time taken by the converter is analyzed through the performance advisor tool in MATLAB software. ODE23s provides the quickest response, while ODE45 has the highest accuracy.

articleTitle: Improving Cabin Comfort With Smart Auto-Flap HVAC Control
abstract: In a country like India with tropical weather, cabin temperature of passenger vehicle (PV) plays a significant role in customer delight. As per our study, 90% of PV users in India prefer to use the recirculation mode in the Heating, ventilation, and Air-conditioning (HVAC) system to safeguard themselves from the elevated levels of pollution outside the vehicle (in-particular PM2.5). Owing to the use of recirculation mode for a prolonged period, the CO₂ level in the cabin is likely to increase causing discomfort to the occupants. Continuous exposure to high concentration of CO₂ (Over 2500 ppm) could result in headache, dizziness, and nausea. In this work, we studied the in-cabin concentration of CO₂ & PM2.5 under different test conditions like city driving, highway, off-road, re-circulation mode, fresh air mode, etc., Based on the results & considering the ideal exposure to in-cabin CO₂ and PM2.5, a HVAC auto-flap mechanism is developed to enhance cabin comfort for the PV users.

articleTitle: Improving Battery Performance Using Optislang Based Model Calibration of Newman P2d Model
abstract: The efficiency of Li-ion 21700 class cells is studied under various electrochemical, thermal, and geometrical properties. An advanced automated workflow was developed using Newman P2D model and Non-Linear Programming by Quadratic Lagrangian (NLPQL) algorithm. Using this workflow, optimized set of battery design parameters were estimated. With the optimized parameters, the cell performance was validated against the test data [7]. The effect of discharge rates 0.5C, 1C, 2C and 3C on battery electrochemical and thermal behavior was studied. The critical parameters considered in this study are Maximum Solid Li+ concentration, Stoichiometry at 0% and 100%, Reference rate constant at both the positive and negative electrodes of the battery. The effect of tab configuration on potential loss analysed, results showed that with continuous tab potential loss is very less compared to single- and double-tab configurations. Using this automated workflow engineers can easily and quickly size the batteries from classic 18650 to new 21700 or any other type of batteries.

articleTitle: Isolated DC Microgrid Operation with Hybridization of PV, FC, and Battery
abstract: Hybrid power systems based on fuel cells, photo-voltaic (PV) sources, and batteries have emerged as promising solutions for clean and reliable power generation. This paper presents an investigation into the integration of these technologies to enhance energy efficiency, improve energy management, and maximize the utilization of renewable energy sources. The proposed work covers the modelling, control, energy management, and operation of a hybrid system comprising a fuel cell, photo-voltaic (PV) system, and battery energy storage system (BESS). In addition to this reduces the current ripple which is suitable for renewable energy sources like (PV and FC). A grid-tied hybrid system employs a primary source of renewable distributed generation, consisting of both photovoltaic (PV) panels and a fuel cell (FC), with a secondary source being a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS).

articleTitle: Solar-to-Vehicle Charging with Maximum Power Point Tracking using Super-Twisting Controller
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for max-imizing power point tracking (MPPT) in solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, specifically designed for charging electric vehicles (EVs). The approach incorporates a super-twisting controller (STC) to achieve efficient MPPT in the PV system. The STC is utilized to effectively regulate the power output of PV panels by accurately tracking their maximum power points. In contrast to conventional sliding mode controllers, STCs reduces chattering and provides better tracking. As a potential renewable energy solution, the proposed technique offers a convenient method of enhancing the power output of photovoltaic systems. To evaluate its effectiveness under various conditions such as irradiance and temperature fluctuations, the proposed method is compared against the conventional perturb and observe (P&O) MPPT technique. Finally, the effectiveness of the suggested method is demonstrated through comparative simulations, highlighting its advantages in the presence of environmental disturbances.

articleTitle: Passive Cell Equalization & State of Charge Estimation Using Coulomb Counting Approach
abstract: The veracity of a battery model and SOC estimation has a profound impact on the control strategy of a vehicle management system and electric vehicle performance, which is critical for efficient battery management and increasing vehicle reliability. The intent of this project is to extend battery longevity through cell balancing, which is instrumental in preserving battery life. This paper examines the merits and drawbacks of various SOC estimation techniques, as well as the principles, analysis of battery pack in MATLAB/ Simulink, implementation of Coulomb Counting Method and research progress of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SoC}$</tex> estimation algorithms and passive cell balancing, with the goal of providing references for future researchers.

articleTitle: Design Optimization in Automotive Product Development Using AI/ML Algorithms
abstract: The use of physical testing and simulation process for product development of effective design is a well-established practice in industry. Engineers rely on this process to explore the feasible design space and optimize product for future design configurations. Designers and researchers can use the data from existing designs to develop future designs. In this context, this paper presents an effective solution by using physical test and simulation data for day-to-day design problems such as Plastic Snap design and Chassis Section deflection. A high degree of accuracy is achieved in validating test data using machine learning algorithms. By using ML algorithms in product design, we can optimize the parameters in a shorter time & reduce development cost.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Current Control Improved Performance on SRM Drive for Electric Vehicles
abstract: The switched reluctance motor (SRM) is a prominent electrical machine for variable speed drive to minimize the overall cost of on-road traction motor applications. This machine has a few drawbacks: torque ripple and flux ripple. However, the classical Model Predictive Control (MPC) model using torque and flux control state variables is more complex to predict the accurate value and can minimize cost function error as a result of high torque ripple. On the other hand, the existing MPC gives high torque ripples due to the improper selection of switching states techniques of the converter, which can result in high torque ripples. Therefore, this paper proposed a Model Predictive Current Control (MPCC) using single current control variables without a weighting factor to mitigate torque ripple further. The cost function error can be minimized by selecting the converter's optimal switching state. The proposed strategy is verified and validated using MATLAB/Simulink. The detailed result discusses the response of torque, flux, and speed of SRM. The MPCC-operated SRM drive experimental results are shown to prove the effective minimization of torque ripples in the proposed MPCC.

articleTitle: Explicit Dynamic Optimization for Battery Using Equivalent Static Load Method (ESLM)
abstract: The automotive market is shifting towards development of carbon neutralization techniques, hence there is an exponential increase in the demand for electric vehicles. The driving system in an electric vehicle consists of electric machine, battery, and power electronics (including charging system). The battery system is an assembly of various units - cover, modules, busbar, BMS, floor integrated with cooling system and housing, which undergoes various assembly and functional loads. There are other loads primarily, NVH loads from roads and Crash loads. The impact of crash in a battery could be catastrophic. We can deform module containing lithium-ion cells, and this event is called intrusion that leads to thermal run-away. The scope of work is to develop Explicit dynamic Optimization method for Battery using ESLM to reduce the intrusion levels and optimize part stiffness. The ESLM used here is a combination of shape & size optimization for effective design of battery.

articleTitle: Battery Cooling System Optimization for Battery Electric Bus
abstract: Electric vehicles are gaining significant importance due to the depletion and adverse impact of fossil fuels on the environment. Electric vehicles are preferred as it is not dependent on fossil fuel and have zero tail pipe emissions. Many automobile manufacturers are shifting from internal combustion engine to electric vehicles. Battery being the main source of energy to power these vehicles, its life and performance are critical to vehicle life & performance. Battery Thermal Management design is key to ensure life & performance of the Vehicle. Efficiency of battery cooling system is dependent on proper selection of refrigeration system, coolant flow, its uniformity & cooling circuit configuration with multiple packs in application like Bus. In recent times, 1D simulations have gained a high importance to conduct thermal simulations of vehicle and to understand the complex interactions. 1D simulation reduces the product development time and helps in bringing quicker products to the market. Coolant flow and Thermal performance are critical for battery and vehicle performance, so accurate prediction is critical at the initial product development stage. The existing layout was analyzed, and the proposed layout was simplified with the use of restrictor to achieve the uniform flow and uniform temperature through all the battery packs. Physical testing was done, and the results were compared with the simulation.

articleTitle: Accelerating the development of Software Defined Vehicles through Innovative Collaboration across the Industry
abstract: Today's Mobility Customers are evolving to differentiate their Vehicle value by its response and customization, to their needs in a digital ecosystem. Software is rapidly defining future Smart e-mobility solutions to meet these aspirations. Architectures are seen to transform to Zone oriented high performance systems. Further the hardware layer is to be abstracted from containerized application-based software. This enables the use of outsourced applications which can be upgraded or customized independently. Inter-operability vide standardized middleware and interface protocols along with connectivity to Edge and Cloud services require collaboration among the stake holders. The application of AI-ML empowered Digital twins and collaborative digital tools will enable continuous improvement with DevOps, which is transferred by OTA upgrades throughout the Product Life cycle. Functional safety and Cyber security also require close alignment and accountability with key partners. The paper highlights and illustrates collaboration processes necessary across the industry for accelerating the transformation to Software Defined Vehicles with different levels of autonomy.

articleTitle: An Advance Model of Electric Vehicle for EV Charger Evaluation
abstract: The global transition towards environmentally friendly transportation is steering us away from conventional vehicles toward electric ones [3]. Charging infrastructure is at the core of electric vehicle (EV) adoption, and addressing issues during the charging process [7] is pivotal. This research endeavours to create an advanced and compact model of an electric vehicle, specifically designed for testing EV chargers. Presently, there is a dearth of cost-effective devices capable of systematically assessing charger functionality. When attempting to charge an EV through a charger and an unexpected fault interrupts the process, determining whether the issue lies with the vehicle or the charger [4] can be challenging. Traditional troubleshooting methods entail labour-intensive, manual inspection of each charger component, consuming considerable time. However, this research work aims to develop a system that can swiftly identify charger faults within a mere 2-minute timeframe. It's important to note that this research exclusively focuses on detecting and addressing faults within the EV charger system [6], with no concern for issues on the electric vehicle side.

articleTitle: An Isolated Three-Port Converter with Multi- Level PFC Converter for Hybrid Charging Application
abstract: Research into power electronic based converters is essential in order to provide high-power, low-cost, and reliable charging solutions for the EV battery as EVs become increasingly popular. A five-level power factor correction (PFC) converter, a series resonant converter (SRC), and a dual active bridge (DAB) converter are presented in this study to form an isolated hybrid three-port converter with the capabilities to accomplish the aforementioned goals. The suggested converter's three-port architecture lessens the overall number of parts, which in turn reduces the system's price and complexity. Multilevel rectifier (MLR) implementation at the input stage improves the quality of the input voltage waveform while lowering the voltage requirements for power switches. A straightforward decoupled control strategy based on pulse width modulation (PWM) and phase shift was devised to regulate power flow across all three ports simultaneously. The system is modeled in MATLAB/Simulink and verified in the lab through experiments.

articleTitle: Drive Cycle-Based Loss Minimization Strategies for Induction Motor Drives in Electrified Vehicles
abstract: A wide range of speed and torque demands are imposed on the electric motor drive systems for automotive traction applications. Reduction of losses in the traction motor is a key to enhancing the overall efficiency of the e-drive system. However, loss reduction becomes a challenge under such widely varying conditions, due to operating point dependencies. Particularly, drive cycles comprising of rapidly varying vehicle load patterns pose additional difficulty in the design of loss reducing algorithms. A model-based, offline loss minimization method is presented in this paper, by performing a constrained optimization of the operating point-dependent loss function. A control strategy using a varying motor flux approach is adopted. Detailed simulation studies are carried out on a rotor-field orientation-controlled induction motor drive system, to demonstrate the performance of the loss minimization method for various load patterns. Results indicate that the control algorithm works effectively for drive cycles involving modal behavior but exhibits limited performance in drive cycles consisting of dominantly transient behavior. Further, use of this algorithm is restricted to a speed limit in the flux-weakening region which curtails the motor flux to a maximum permissible profile.

articleTitle: Isolated Single Switch High Frequency Inverter for Wireless Charging of Light Electric Vehicles
abstract: Reduction in power conversion stages, low cost, less volume, and miniaturization, supports the development and commercialization of Wireless power transfer (WPT). This work details the THD reduction and input Power Factor Correction (PFC) for EV applications. To address the supply power quality problems and reduce the number of switches used, a single-switched boost-based isolated Flyback converter is proposed as the forepart converter. Reducing the quantity of switches leads to a simplification in pulse generation, resulting in decreased losses and an overall improvement in efficiency. The recommended single-stage, single-switched converter at the front-end operates in Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM), offering integral Power Factor Correction (PFC). This converter is specifically designed to deliver 3.7kW of output power at a resonant frequency of 85kHz and an output voltage of 400V. Utilizing MATLAB/Simulink simulations, the proposed front-end converter is evaluating the performance, achieving a maximum efficiency of 96.85%.

articleTitle: Designing Functional Safety Architecture for FCEV Vehicles
abstract: Fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs), electric vehicles (EVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and hydrogen internal combustion engine vehicles (H2ICEs) are expected to have significant growth in the future due to the implementation of stringent emission norms. FCEVs have a unique role in the future of transportation as they produce no emissions. Instead of relying on a battery for electricity, FCEVs generate power through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen in a fuel cell stack, emitting only pure water in the exhaust. This makes them a reliable solution to the global warming problem. Additionally, refueling the hydrogen tank of an FCEV takes less than five minutes, unlike charging a battery. However, it is crucial to ensure the safety of fuel cell vehicles against high-pressure hydrogen gas and high voltage. Therefore, a functional safety architecture for FCEVs must be developed. This paper aims to describe one of the design approaches for the functional safety architecture of the hydrogen storage control unit (HSCU) in accordance with the ISO26262 standard and GTR13 standard.

articleTitle: Grid-Integrated Bidirectional EV Charger for G2V-V2G Mode with Optimized Power Quality
abstract: The rapid expansion of the electric vehicle (EV) market has several prospects for expanding the use of clean energy in the automobile industry. In order to keep up with the surging interest in EVs, there has to be a concentrated effort to improve the charging infrastructure. This study describes a concept which integrates single-phase grid with bidirectional EV battery charger having G2V-V2G (Grid-to-Vehicle-Vehicle-to-Grid) capabilities. The 2-stage bidirectional EV charger system has been modeled in MATLAB Simulink to enhance the power quality. The simulation study showcased that a genetic algorithm (GA) optimized EV charger controller had a lower total harmonic distortion (THD) content in grid current when compared to EV charger that did not have an optimized controller.

articleTitle: Electric Motor Copper Winding Stiffness Calculation Method by FEA Approach
abstract: Electric motor is a key component of an electric vehicle. Electric motors consist of 3 primary components - Rotor, stator, and housing - stator / housing are fixed parts and rotor is the rotating part. Electric motors work on the principle of magnetic flux, thereby, making the function of copper winding as a primary efficiency factor in both stator and rotor. The electric motor rotor experiences high centrifugal loading due to high rotational speed, and hence, winding in the rotor are more complex and necessary to be structurally integral. The copper wire winding with a layer of enamel coating is fused with varnish to form a composite like structure around the stack. Ways to predict the winding mechanical behavior which influences the structural integrity of the copper winding shall be studied with an equivalent FEA approach with better correlation to the physical tests.

articleTitle: Power Control and Efficiency Enhancement Topology for Dual Receiver Wireless Power Transfer EV Quasi-Dynamic Charging
abstract: A Quasi-Dynamic Wireless Inductive Power Transfer (QDWIPT) system for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging applications, benefits from user-friendly charging with reduced charging duration and limited battery capacity for long-distance travel. This article proposes the Dual receiver power control and Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) enhancement topology for the QDWIPT system. This topology inculcates; a half-active bridge rectifier for Dual pickup Receiver (Rx) coils and battery charging power controlled by a DC-DC converter in the secondary unit. The power controller design and control strategies are based on dual receiver topology and the DC-DC chopper model for an effective battery charging process. The dual pick-up decoupled feature coils are placed at optimal distance, with a resonant compensator to minimize the cross-coupling effect in the wireless coupling region. The half-active rectifiers maximize the transmitting efficiency of the dual receiver coil topology with the power control method. This proposed QDWIPT topology is experimentally investigated for a 3.3 kW prototype and power-controlled battery charging is discussed in this article.

articleTitle: Passive Balancing of Battery using Coulomb Counting and Kalman Filter based SoC Estimation
abstract: The balancing of a cell in a battery pack comprises of controlling the charging and discharging of the respective cell to keep it at the same potential as of the other cells in the battery pack. The paper describes the process of balancing a cell by taking the State of Charge (SoC) of the cell into consideration rather than the conventional voltage of the cell. The estimation of the SoC is done by applying Kalman Filter to the measurement. This usage of Kalman Filter helps in estimating the SoC very accurately and thus helping in balancing the cell more effectively and thereby improving the overall health of the battery pack.

Author Keywords: SoC (State of Charge). SoH (State of Health)

articleTitle: Method for Identifying Movements of Vehicle Body
abstract: This research paper gives an insight towards identifying the vehicle body movements. The accuracy of projecting from 2-D to 3-D for each image pixel to its corresponding point in the real world depends on having precise knowledge of the location of the camera and its tilt angles with respect to the surroundings. The end-of-line calibration is performed while the car is unloaded. There are countless possible variations in the vehicle's load conditions which causes different camera positions and tilt angles result. Because of this, the projection's transformation is inaccurate, and the objects appear to be closer or farther apart than they really are. The problem solution aims to identify the height and the tilt angles of the vehicle at standstill and during driving scenarios. The advantage is we can use this before the ignition of the vehicle, when the load changes due to addition of passengers and luggage's.

articleTitle: Design for Disassembly: A key to achieving a Circular Economy for EV Battery Systems
abstract: This paper focuses on designing electric vehicle (EV) battery systems for a circular economy, prioritizing reusing and recycling battery subcomponents. Design for disassembly is a crucial principle enabling closed-loop systems where subcomponents can be disassembled, reused, or recycled. The authors emphasize the importance of disassembling battery subcomponents and suggest solutions for interfaces that prioritize easy disassembly and non-destructive separation. The paper proposes delaying the recycling stage of batteries, enabling the reuse of functional subcomponents beyond their original automotive application. Overall, the paper emphasizes the importance of Design for Disassembly in achieving a sustainable and efficient circular economy for EV battery systems.

articleTitle: Inner loop Current Control Techniques for Speed controlled Double Inverter fed Wound Rotor Induction Motor Drive
abstract: The growing electrification of transport has prompted researchers to examine control methods for various electric machines. One such machine is double-inverter fed wound rotor induction machine (DI-WRIM). Field oriented control (FOC), direct torque control (DTC) and current oriented control (COC) techniques are often employed for this machine. Proportional+integral (PI) based FOC is the most popular closed loop control for a DI-WRIM drive. This paper tends to explore the DI-WRIM drive's performance with proportional+resonant control (PR) and hysteresis control. Further, the comparative results are presented for all the techniques. The efficacy of these techniques is validated through suitable simulation and experimental results.

Author Keywords: Double-inverter fed wound rotor induction machine (DI- WRIM)

articleTitle: Security of Connected Cars that Promise Zero Accidents
abstract: Road traffic accidents result in the death of approximately 1.3 million people worldwide each year, and 20 to 50 million people suffer injuries. The goal of zero accidents on the road is becoming more achievable thanks to the advent of connected vehicles. As more and more vehicles become connected, the potential for zero accidents becomes increasingly realistic. However, these possibilities will also present new problems for the automakers. One such is cyber security in the reason because software flaws could jeopardize the security of connected car features and systems. This paper sheds light on another possible way of preventing cyber-attacks by isolating the cloud from cellular traffic in connected cars architecture and appending the cloud with cloud Access Security Brokers to provide security and control access to cloud resources. We outline ways to various access control modules in the architecture.

articleTitle: Active Cell Balancing and SOC Estimation Using Coulomb Counting in Python
abstract: An electric vehicle's performance and control strategy depend on how precise the battery model and SOC estimation are. These factors are crucial for effective battery management and enhancing vehicle reliability. In this paper, firstly, the State of Charges (SOCs) of each cell is estimated using Python. Later, a MATLAB model was used to find the SOCs of each cell and compared the values obtained from Python. Secondly, to perform Active Cell Balancing, a MATLAB model was built comprising of four cells linked in series. The energy from higher cells was shifted to lower ones to equalize the SOCs, and optimal results were obtained.

articleTitle: Influence of Charging-Pad Design Parameters on Self-Inductance Variation with Air-Gap and Coupling Coefficient for IPT in Low Clearance EVs
abstract: Ferromagnetic material used in the construction of charging-pads for Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) systems in Electric Vehicles (EVs) causes self-inductance to vary with the air-gap between the pads, resulting in a mistuned system and sub-optimal performance. The phenomenon of self-inductance variation is more pronounced in IPT systems for EVs with low ground clearance, where it increases non-linearly as the air-gap reduces. This paper systematically analyzes the impact of critical design parameters on self-inductance variation in charging-pads. The parameters considered are the number of coil turns (and corresponding outer diameter) and dimensions of ferrites with symmetric and asymmetric transmitter and receiver coils, assuming a constant cross-sectional area, inter-turn distance, and inner diameter of the coils. Although the study considers circular spiral coils, the conclusions can be extended to other coil types. This paper uses ANSYS Maxwell 3D simulations to compare the impact of various design parameters on self-inductance variation in charging pads, considering an air-gap range of 3cm to 18cm. The paper includes plots showing self-inductances and coupling coefficients versus air-gap, and provides preliminary experimental validation. This work can provide valuable guidelines to IPT system engineers for optimizing charging pad design to minimize the self-inductance variation, thereby improving the system performance.

articleTitle: Versatile On-Board Power Processor for BLDC & IM Driven Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper proposes a versatile on-board power converter for BLDC and induction motor-driven electric vehicles. The single converter can be operated in charging as well as in motoring mode of operation. The proposed converter transforms between charging and propulsion operation with the help of electromechanical relays and some passive components. In its charging operation, it maintains the unity power factor at the source terminal and charges the battery with a constant current constant voltage (CC-CV) algorithm. In its propulsion operation, it can drive either the brushless DC motor or the Induction motor with different switching logic. It provides the source voltages to the power support of the cabin in charging and propulsion operation. The concept is validated for 300 W and 500 W during charging and motoring mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Sustaining Steady Voltage in Hybrid Fuel Cell and Battery Power Systems Amid Fluctuating Load Conditions
abstract: The rapid growth of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has spurred a surge in energy demand, emphasizing the imperative need for renewable energy sources. One such energy source that can be integrated into EVs to meet their charging requirements is the fuel cell (FC). However, the integration of FCs with EVs necessitates the use of power electronics converters. These converters play a vital role in matching the load voltage, as the FC output voltage tends to decrease under higher load demand. To enhance the performance of FCs and their integration with batteries, this study introduces a novel state-flow control mechanism. The primary goal of this research is to address the challenges posed by decreasing FC output voltage in response to higher load demands. To evaluate the proposed solution, a hybrid input source is supplied under three different load conditions: low, medium, and high. Extensive validation is conducted, with simulation results obtained through MATLAB Simulink. Additionally, an experimental setup has been established in LABVIEW, tailored specifically for fuel cell operations. The findings of this study encompass a detailed analysis of voltage, current, and efficiency under all three load conditions. These results provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of the proposed state-flow control mechanism in optimizing the performance of both FCs and batteries, making them well-suited to meet the escalating energy demands of Electric Vehicles.

articleTitle: India EV Energy Ecosystem – Challenges … Future Roadmap
abstract: The global transportation sector is being challenged for carbon and other toxic gas emissions and is in the middle of a rapid transition from traditional technologies (i.e., internal combustion propulsion) to a more sustainable option. Considering current viable technologies, electrification of propulsion has emerged as leading alternate option. China and Europe are leading the way in this transition, with the USA and Japan not far behind. India though has taken a balanced approach through its FAME initiative thus encouraging transition to electric vehicles and holds ambitions for significant movement towards electrification by 2030. Transportation (Passenger and Cargo) had seen an organic growth spanning more than a century and associated through this development is its acceptance and an evolved eco system surrounding fossil fuel technologies. Disruption of this Juggernaut towards Electrification of Transportation carries benefits such as perceived Lifecycle Carbon footprint reduction, related Crude Import reduction, and Forex Savings. Electrification of Transportation is a multi-dimensional approach involving key areas such as (i)Government Initiatives and Regulations, (ii)Advanced Battery Technology and Material logistics, (iii)Renewable and Sustainable Energy (iv)Transfer Grid Systems (v)Charging Infrastructure (vi)Smart and Connected networks and (vii) Vehicle models are available in an affordable and acceptable range of configurations. This paper brings to forefront how Ecosystem is expected to evolve towards successful market accommodation. The current challenge for mankind is to create a Sustainable and Organic “Electrification” ecosystem in an accelerated timeframe. Success depends on disruptions with minimal impact on transportation.

articleTitle: Transformerless Dual Input Dual Output DC-DC Converter for Electric Vehicle Application
abstract: A Transformerless dual input dual output (TDIDO) DC-DC converter for electrical vehicle application is projected in this paper. The proposed TDIDO converter is designed for utilizing PV and fuel cells to charge the battery of EVs. The TDIDO DC-DC Converter has a dual input system, with one input from a solar PV array and the other from a fuel cell. It offers several advantages for the converter's design and operation, including the reduction of multiple power conversions, minimizing the number of components required, and the ability to boost voltage. The working of the converter, analytical waveform, loss breakdown analysis, simulation results, etc., are deliberated in the paper. A comparison of conventional converters is conveyed in the literature; the TDIDO DC-DC converter uses one diode, one inductor, two capacitors, and three switches.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Renewable Generation and Battery Energy Storage System for Electric Vehicles Considering Energy Management Strategy
abstract: This paper proposes the optimum capacity of renewable based energy system considering Solar PV, Wind turbines and Battery energy storage for meeting plugin-in Electric vehicles (PEV) load requirements in a case study of Ahmedabad city region, India. The technical and economic analysis have been performed for various combinations of the component of integrated energy system. These combinations include: (a) solar/wind/battery, (b) solar/battery, and (c) wind/battery. The objective function is to reduce energy costs and the possibility of minimizing power outages by peak shaving and proper energy management. The uncertainties associated with PEV such as arrival time, departure time, and initial state of charge have been considered in searching the optimal solutions. A novel Giza pyramid construction algorithm (GPCA) is implemented considering the annual PEV load profile and actual yearly solar irradiance and wind speed data on hourly basis. The simulation results show that the GPCA achieves the desired objectives with high accuracy and resilience. The superiority of the solution provided by the Giza Pyramid Algorithm is proven by comparing the results obtained using Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA) and Moth Flame Optimization (MFO). The research findings will provide valuable insights for researchers to determine the optimal strategy for powering PEV load using a multi-energy system approach.

articleTitle: A Statistical Approach to Estimate the Transient Torsional Load on EV Driveline Due to a Sudden Vehicle Wheel Slip-Grab Event
abstract: Transportation vehicles may experience very high transient loads on the driveline under certain driving conditions. Although such extremely severe conditions are rare, designing systems for the theoretical worst possible scenarios will lead to an over-designed system. Wheel slip-grab is one such abusive maneuver which can lead to high driveline torsional load due to sudden change in traction. Previous studies which considered similar wheel slip-grab maneuvers covered sensitivity analysis, system MDOF model correlation with test data, however, a need to create a simple mathematical model that provides insights to the phenomenon and consideration to probability of occurrence of such peak torque is identified. Hence, in this paper, an approach is presented to achieve a balance between risk and robustness by simulating a complete driveline system for wheel slip-grab scenario. Key design and noise factors were varied to obtain peak transient torque on the driveline in probabilistic manner using Monte-Carlo analysis. The outcome of this analysis is beneficial for quantifying risk and evaluating possible mitigation strategies through controls such as wheel slip control.

articleTitle: Power Factor Correction in Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer System Using Primary Side Phase Shift Control Technique
abstract: In conventional setups, power factor correction (PFC) for wireless power transfer systems typically involves utilizing a boost converter. However, this article introduces a novel approach by proposing primary side converter phase shift control for power factor correction in bidirectional wireless power transfer applications. The primary phase shift angle in this approach is responsible for regulating the battery charging current/voltage within the Series-series compensated Wireless bidirectional Power Transfer (BDWPT) system. The innovative primary side phase shift control eliminates the need for chopper/boost converter circuits for PFC, streamlining the circuit complexity. Additionally, the bidirectional power flow becomes feasible with the phase-synchronized converter. These systems integrate various functionalities, including PFC, current shaping, Total Harmonic Distortion, and power management, all under a single control mechanism based on duty-cycle control that operates in close proximity to the resonance frequency. The BDWPT system is meticulously designed and simulated using the MATLAB/Simulink model. Also, the experimental investigations are performed to validate the developed model.

Author Keywords: Phase Shift Control Power Factor Correction

articleTitle: A Framework for Low-Cost Autonomous Mobility Platform to Retrofit Electric Vehicles
abstract: Autonomous Driving and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems features are continuously evolving and maturing towards fully Autonomous Vehicles. Autonomous Mobility Platforms play an important role in conceptualization, design, test, deployment, and upgrade of sub-systems in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems and Autonomous Driving systems. Off-the-shelf platforms are available for research and academic purposes but are proprietary, expensive, and inflexible. In-house development of an Autonomous Mobility Platform by retrofitting an existing vehicle is a viable option to realize Autonomous Vehicles. The inhouse platform can be cost effective, open, modular, reusable, and customizable. This paper presents a framework comprising architecture, design, and implementation features of such a standalone Autonomous Mobility Platform to retrofit existing vehicles.

articleTitle: A G2V and V2V Competency Bidirectional Dual Active Bridge Converter
abstract: This work introduces an isolated converter dual-active-bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter-specific dead band proportional-integral (PI) current controller for the bidirectional operation. The controller provided in this work utilizes pulse width as an additional control variable, boosting the single-phase shift (SPS) modulation technique, in contrast to standard single-phase shift (SPS) modulation systems that mainly rely on a 90-degree phase shift ratio. With this new method, bidirectional power transmission may be conducted with accurate tracking of the current reference during a single switching cycle and seamless switching between the two directions. The controller efficiently achieves Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) and Zero Current Switching (ZCS) by using a PI controller and hysteresis band to manage PWM pulses, eliminating switching losses and increasing overall converter efficiency. The results of experiments obtained during the converter's transient processes prove the higher dynamic performance of the proposed dead band current controller, which shows its simplicity and ease of implementation. Additionally, grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) power flow control's effectiveness and successful validation through 1 kW prototype experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of Partial Power Processing Converter Architectures for EV Fast Charging Station
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to analyze and compare various partial power processing converter (PPPC) architectures for electric vehicle (EV) fast chargers. Detailed mathematical analyses of the possible PPPC architectures are presented. The comparison of these architectures is done in terms of converter input and output current and voltages, overall system efficiency, and partial power processed ratio. Based on this analysis, the best possible architecture for a 350 kW-rated EV fast charger is suggested with respect to the most suitable DC-link voltage. The simulation analysis is done in the MATLAB environment.

articleTitle: Protecting Passengers and Data: The Importance of a Consistent Process from TARA to Testing
abstract: The automotive industry's rapid transition to software-defined vehicles (SDVs) presents a complex cybersecurity landscape. With nearly every vehicle function based on software, the attack surface has grown exponentially. With each line of code added, the potential for vulnerabilities grows. In addition, modern vehicles communicate via numerous interfaces, including the Internet, Bluetooth, diagnostic ports and more. This diverse connectivity creates a maze of potential entry points for cyber attackers. In addition, the interconnectedness of vehicle components means that a breach in one area can have far-reaching consequences, impacting critical functions and occupant safety. To effectively address these challenges, the use of new methods and technologies for early threat detection is essential. Traditional approaches to cybersecurity are no longer sufficient. A proactive stance is required to defend against cyber threats from the outset. In addition to identifying threats, it is equally important to test the effectiveness of countermeasures. This includes simulating potential attacks to determine if they could realistically occur and if mitigation strategies are robust enough to neutralize them.

articleTitle: A Seven-Level Single-Phase Shared Leg Toroidal Transformer Based Inverter For Grid-Connected Applications
abstract: The present paper introduces a 7-level single-phase shared leg toroidal transformer-based inverter for grid-connected applications. It uses optimal device count compared to conventional topologies such as a single DC source, eight semiconductor switches, and three toroidal transformers to get a seven-level symmetrical output voltage. Besides, the selective harmonic elimination (SHE) technique demands solving the transcendental equations, hence it becomes difficult for real-time closed-loop operation when connected to the grid. However, these transcendental equations are converted to a closed-loop control system with reduced memory size and get switching angles to achieve precise control to eliminate the required harmonics. The proposed configuration is verified using MATLAB/SIMULINK software and validated through a real-time simulator (OPAL-RT).

articleTitle: A Mechanism to Determine Fast Charging Protocol of Battery
abstract: The ever growing need to decarbonize the economy is forcing policy makers to frame regulations favoring sustainability. The transportation sector being carbon-intensive is under heavy scrutiny of the policy makers. To provide sustainable transportation solution to the customers, automotive manufacturers are developing Electric Vehicles (EV). However, the huge charging time required to charge the EVs is a major hindrance for the wide-spread acceptance of EVs. This study proposes a methodology to achieve fast charging of batteries. Charging time is targeted to be reduced while ensuring the operational and practical constraints on charging. The C-rate for charging is the operational constraint considered. The practical constraints include the temperature and temperature rise rate of the battery as they need to be maintained within well-defined range. The charging protocol obtained using the proposed approach satisfies all the operational and practical constraints and the charging time is 1430 seconds with negligible capacity fade. Comparison with two other charging strategies - aggressive and slow charging protocols indicate the drawbacks with these approaches establishing the utility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Wide Bandgap Devices for Parallel Hybrid Wireless Charging Systems
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) has been widely adopted globally despite its high cost and intolerance to mis-alignment. Alternatively, capacitive power transfer (CPT)-based charging systems can be utilized, as they are misalignment tolerant, less expensive, and lighter. Nevertheless, the power density and efficiency of the CPT chargers are less than the IPT chargers. This paper proposes a grid connected dual-stage parallel hybrid wireless power transfer (HWPT) system to enhance power capacity and efficiency with better misalignment tolerance for electric vehicle charging applications. Also, the design and operating cost estimation process is presented by using the correlations between the cost and performance indices of wide bandgap devices. To validate the proposed system, a 3.3 kW parallel HWPT charger with a constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) charging control technique is designed and simulated on the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Multi-leg Inverter Fed Roadway Wirelessly Powered Charging System
abstract: Resonant Inductive Power Transmission (RIPT) is an advanced wireless technology for charging EV batteries, offering a safe and practical solution. RIPT systems require high-power transmission, reliability, durability, and cost-effectiveness to enable highway charging. This study presents a fault-tolerant multi-legged quasi-dynamic wireless charging system, aiming to reduce costs by utilizing individual legs of the inverter for each Transmitter (Tx) coil. In a leg fault, a fast-acting changeover switch redirects the Tx coil to an adjacent leg. Fuses/Circuit Breakers are integrated into each leg for protection during fault conditions, ensuring system safety. Additionally, each Tx coil has a sensor that triggers charging when a Receiver (Rx) coil passes over the charging path, facilitating efficient power transfer. Driving the Tx coil is achieved by configuring each leg of the converter as a half-bridge inverter circuit, enabling effective power transfer and control. In this study, the misalignment effect is not considered. The proposed system is verified using MATLAB simulation and results are analyzed.

articleTitle: An Improved Vehicle-to-Vehicle Wireless Power Transfer System for Electric Vehicle Applications Using Reconfigurable Two-Phase Transmitter
abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) energy transfer is a necessary topology in the Electric Vehicle (EV) charging field. The connectivity between EVs using rigid cables adds difficulties while making the connectivity due to its weight. The recent advancements in Wireless power transfer (WPT) technology give comfortable connectivity between EVs for energy sharing. In WPT, the coupling between the transmitter pad (TP) and the receiver pad (RP) plays a noticeable role in the power transfer efficiency (PTE) and transmission distance. In this article, a reconfigurable two-phase circular transmitter pad improves the coupling factor (K). The impact of the proposed two-phase coil on the coupling factor is verified with the ANSYS-MAXWELL simulation tool. The cross-coupling effects due to the dual transmitter are minimized by phase-shifted excitation of the relay coil and capacitor. An improvement of 4.7% in PTE has been achieved in the implemented charging system with two-phase coil-based WPT by performing the energy sharing between two 24V, 28Ah batteries.

articleTitle: High Power Density Fuel Cell Systems for Commercial Vehicles
abstract: Fuel cells represent a promising yet complex solution for achieving zero-emission heavy-duty commercial vehicles. AVL has designed a versatile 156 kW fuel cell system, leveraging it to create an efficient fuel cell powertrain for long-haul semitrailer tractors. This system aligns with industry expectations regarding longevity, performance, fuel efficiency, driving range, and cost-effectiveness in terms of acquisition and operation.

articleTitle: Virtual Road Load Data Simulation
abstract: Development of transmission involves generation of duty cycle, for bench level durability evaluation. For transmission RLD, vehicle is driven in various conditions for several hundred kilometers equipped with numerous sensors and design intended components. This paper provides the methodology to overcome these challenges by virtual RLD using simulation software like AVL Route studio and VSM. By giving vehicle parameters as input to the software, we can generate data with good accuracy for different routes and thereby reducing the development cost & time with less manpower. This has added advantage of eliminating fuel utilization (no carbon emission). This paper provides complete detail about development of vehicle model, GPS routes with speed limit, live traffic condition and driver aggression level to simulate exact conditions as that of real world. Methodology adopted in the paper can be used for all types of transmission with no restriction of geographical conditions and requirement of vehicle at early stage of transmission development.

articleTitle: Flux-Barrier Based Rotor Design of Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor with Power Density and Torque ripple Improvement for e-Mobility
abstract: SynRM and PMaSynRM are emerging as promising alternatives to the use of PMSMs for e-mobility but have compromised performance characteristics and lower power density. Use of rare-earth free motors for electric vehicles (EVs) with low torque ripple being of paramount importance. This paper proposes a new design approach for ferrite magnets based PMaSynRM by adopting the fluid flux barrier based outer rotor configuration and introduces the phase advanced angle. Using finite element analysis (FEA), magneto-static parametric analysis is performed first to determine the optimum phase advanced angle leading to maximum torque. Subsequently, for reduction of torque ripple, transient simulations are carried out and torque profiles are generated from FEA iteratively by varying the carrier and barrier widths using PSO algorithm. FEA is carried out in Ansys Maxwell to validate the proposed design and is coupled with MATLAB to perform optimization studies. Finally, the rotor design that yields the least torque ripple is chosen as the best design. Later, use of skewed rotor is also proposed to further reduce the torque ripple. The results obtained for the PMaSynRM with the design approach proposed in this paper shows a 100% improvement in the power density in addition to 61% reduction in the torque ripple when compared to one of the recently reported works.

articleTitle: Enhanced Technical Capability for EV and SDV through AI based Functional Competency Assessment
abstract: Auto product and services companies across the globe are facing an uphill task to develop and sustain technical teams as the automotive moves away from a traditional mechanical oriented system. With the influx of electronics, transition to electric mobility and increasingly complex software features, the ‘computer on wheels’ is evolving fast. Companies need the talent in to stay relevant in the ‘future mobility’ areas and they need it now. The challenge of finding the right talent and assessing the candidates is a very time consuming and slow process. We believe that, by changing the hiring and assessment process, organizations can successfully build strong technical teams. An effective use to AI to automate the human involvement in selecting the candidate and ensuring the role-fit can simplify the challenge at hand. Furthermore, AI can provide customized skill gap analysis and create learning maps to further train these engineers. Our AI based assessment enables an experiential hiring process. This converts the interview into a practical assessment thereby removing the interviewer's bias and solely focus on what is essential to deliver in a certain technical role. The experiential hiring process builds a hiring process based on a practical approach. The candidate is exposed to a simulated environment, where-in there are multiple experiments and case studies which are selected from a library of over 200 experiments that our team has evolved over the last 4 years. Our AI-assisted functional competency assessment framework is not only valid for new hiring but also for finding the next roles of existing engineers and for creating their learning roadmaps. Such an approach would empower an engineer to prepare themselves for new roles, such as a Battery Recycling Project Manager, and go through an assessment for that role and learn about what gaps are there and get a learning road map for it.

articleTitle: A Model-Based Lumped Parameter Thermal Network for Online Temperature Estimation of IPMSM in Automotive Applications
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM) are widely used in industrial and automotive systems. The thermal behavior of motor parts impacts the performance of electrical drive systems, and accurate temperature information is vital for system protection and controllability. Replacing temperature sensors with thermal estimation reduces the system cost and improves the system's robustness and reliability. However, due to the complexity of high-fidelity thermal models, real-time estimation algorithms are computationally burdensome. To mitigate this computational burden, this study utilizes the calibratable and scalable 11-node reduced-order lumped-parameter thermal network (LPTN) to estimate critical PMSM temperatures in real-time. The Romer Douglas-Peucker (RDP) method is used in this study to develop surrogate loss models for interior permanent magnet machines (IPMSM). The proposed model can be applied to both transient and steady-state operational conditions. However, the temperature is obtained from averaged power loss calculations over a pre-defined raster rate. MATLAB/Simulink is used to understand the behavior of proposed reduced-order LPTN, which are compared with Motor CAD FEA results and Dyne test results to understand the accuracy of proposed models.

articleTitle: An Improved Electrothermal Modeling of Two-Level Inverter for Electric Vehicle Applications
abstract: IGBT power modules are widely employed in electric vehicle motor drive applications. The thermal behavior of these modules becomes more crucial for designing the cooling system for reliable operation. This paper proposes an RC thermal model of SEMIKRON IGBT-based half-bridge inverter module for analyzing the electrothermal behavior under various operating conditions. The proposed thermal model considers the mutual thermal coupling between the devices and the self-heating phenomena of individual devices inside the power module. The power dissipation and junction thermal effects are investigated with and without power module chip mutual couplings. The electrothermal model is developed using the PLECS software environment and validated the same using a two-level voltage source inverter fed 34 kW PMSM motor EV application. The IGBT power loss and junction temperature profiles are presented for an electric vehicle driving cycle of European (NEDC) regulations.

articleTitle: Bms Fusa –How to Achieve Fusa Compliance for A Wireless Bms Design
abstract: The current trends in automotive development show that the use of wireless technology becomes more and more relevant. In battery development, this wireless technology can be applied to realize data exchange within the Battery Management System (BMS). As the BMS is a functional safety relevant system, there is a need to examine the functional safety compliance of the wireless technology as well.
