This paper intends to present the process and concept of achieving ASIL D compliance in a safety relevant data transfer using a wireless channel between two or more safety compliant elements in a BMS. The safety case and concept for the wireless BMS (wBMS) communication channel has been developed in a collaboration project between Analog Devices Inc. (ADI) and AVL, within the scope of ADI's existing system design and product for automotive use. This safety concept has also been assessed by an independent 3rd party organization and found adequate against the relevant requirements from ISO26262 functional safety standard.

articleTitle: Design of a Bi-Directional Dual Active Bridge Converter for Electric Vehicle Battery Charging
abstract: The increasing demand for EV s stems from the need to reduce fossil fuel dependency and mitigate environmental impacts. Efficient EV battery chargers require high-power converters and optimal charging algorithms. This study uses a Bi-Directional Dual Active Bridge Converter (DAB) with Single-Phase Shift control. The DAB adjusts the transformer's turn ratio to provide a wide output voltage range with a controllable phase shift ratio and duty cycle. It offers isolation, fewer passive components, and enables efficient soft-switching. Steady-state and dynamic analyses are conducted using the Generalized Averaging Technique. Control of DAB is done using a PI controller. Regulation of output voltage and output current is made by adjusting the phase angle of bridges for power flow in both directions MATLAB/SIMULINK simulations explore voltage mode control of the DAB for bi-directional power flow with a 5kW converter.

articleTitle: A System Integrator Perspective for Navigating the Future of Mobility Through Software Driven Vehicles
abstract: Software based differentiation and transformation has been permeating across industries over the last few decades. In the automotive industry, Software-Defined Vehicles are abstracting the hardware from software, and intelligently distributing the compute across in-vehicle and cloud. In this paper, we explore Software-Defined Vehicles from a System Integrator's perspective across three axes of market, technology, and customer life cycle. The market view indicates that customers will pay for the additional value delivered throughout the ownership lifetime. Technically, the shift to software-based differentiation will mean more control through software on standard hardware platforms and finally there will be a multitude of services that the Original Equipment Manufacturer and others in the ecosystem will be able to deliver through constant association with the vehicle. The shift to Software-Defined Vehicles would mean that automakers and other players in the ecosystem must transform themselves to build and deepen their software capabilities. There is clearly promise in the software driven world given the successes that other industries have gained, the auto industry must collaborate and learn to deliver on the promise. The system integrator's view is unique since there is an unbiased view, and an ability to look at industries that have gone through similar technology adoption, and then compare how Software-Defined Vehicles will be adopted.

articleTitle: Harmonic Minimization in Switched-Capacitor Multilevel Inverter Using Improved Grey Wolf Optimization
abstract: This research proposes an innovative 13-level switched capacitor multilevel inverter (SC-MLI) with built-in output voltage boosting capability. To obtain a 13-level boosted voltage output, the proposed SC-MLI employs 12 switches and 2 diodes connected with a single DC power source. The switching sequences in the proposed MLI are generated such that the capacitors are self-balanced and optimum voltage levels are obtained at the output. The 13-level SC-MLI proposed in this paper uses a selective harmonic elimination pulse width modulation (SHE-PWM) technique, based improved grey wolf optimization (IGWO) to determine the switching angles for filtering out the lower order harmonics, such as 5th, 7th, etc from the output voltage. The switching angles for the proposed topology have been calculated using IGWO algorithm. The proposed SC-MLI has been simulated using MATLAB/Simulink and experimentally verified through a 400W prototype using NEXYS 4 DDR FPGA. The efficiency of the proposed SC-MLI is found to be 95% and total harmonics distortion (THD) is within the limits. Further, a comparison is also made between the proposed SC-MLI and the other published SC-MLIs, and it is found that the proposed one demonstrates superior performance in terms of gain, total standing voltage (TSV), and number of active and passive components.

Author Keywords: Selective harmonic elimination pulse width modulation (SHE-PWM)

articleTitle: An Improved ANPC-based 7-level Inverter with Reduced Component and Low TSV for EV Applications
abstract: The low dc-link voltage requirements of active-neutral-point-clamped (ANPC) inverters with voltage-gain capabilities make them attractive. The system's overall efficiency, reliability, and power density are improved by the single-stage dc-to-ac power conversion made possible by these low voltage needs. A high voltage gain of 1.5 has been reported for recent boost type ANPC topologies; nevertheless, this was attained at the cost of severe voltage stress on some of its switches. This work provides an enhanced ANPC topology that maintains the advantages of high voltage gain with less voltage stress and fewer components. The proposed configuration produces a 7-level output voltage with 1.5 times voltage boosting using just one flying capacitor, one dc source, and nine switches. A comparative analysis between the proposed topology and other recent topologies is presented to demonstrate its superiority. Also, experimental testing and measurements are carried out to verify the functionality and performance of the proposed topology across a range of loading conditions.

articleTitle: Homomorphic Encryption Technique in Over the Air (OTA) update in ECUs
abstract: The paper talks about securing software in electric vehicles (EV). With the advancement in the over the air (OTA) technology, there has been increase in potential threats as well. OTA helps the OEMs to update the software in lesser cost and lesser time. However, as it is wireless communication, it is prone to security attacks. OTA consists of several steps and each step is prone to different security attack. The possible security attack area lines are pointed out and discussed in this paper and validated proposed results. The probable threats that can happen during data transfer from cloud to the vehicle main unit (VMU) and VMU to sub units such as but not limited to traction controller. This paper proposes a new type of cipher. It has several benefits that are not limited to confidentiality. Its nature allows calculations to be performed directly on translated data without the need for decryption as opposed to conventional ways. The proposed system helps in reducing the time to market further and provides extra layer of security. It helps in reducing the bigwig attacks as the data is not visible during the computing.

Author Keywords: Homomorphic cryptography and Vehicle main unit

articleTitle: LCC-LCC Compensation based Dual Active Bridge Bidirectional WPT for Electric Vehicle Application
abstract: Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer (BWPT) for EV applications is a viable answer to the impending power grid volatility and charging concerns. The Dual Active Bridge (DAB) stands out because to its properties, which include bidirectional operation (vehicle to grid, vehicle to vehicle, and grid to vehicle) and comparably high efficiency, despite the fact that various isolated DC-DC converter topologies find applications in BWPT. Compensation network topologies like SP, PP, and PS can offer either constant current operation (CCO) or constant voltage operation (CVO). However, these topologies comprise harmonics that lead to high power consumption during charging. This study reports on the LCC-LCC hybrid correction, which aims to offer a constant output with minimal total harmonic distortion (THD) and a smooth transition between CCO and CVO. The DAB with LCC compensation, which offers a broad working range, high power density, and the previously described benefits, is presented in the article. The proposed DAB and LCC-LCC compensation are simulated in the MATLAB environment for a power rating of 3.7kW and achieve an efficiency of 96%. An experimental model was developed for a 3.7kW power rating for comparative analysis.

articleTitle: DSM Based In-Vehicle Cabin Setting
abstract: Automation in nook and corner has brought an enormous amount of comfort for customers. Mirrors play a vital role in driving a vehicle. It is important to have proper mirror positions and other cabin settings, subjective to the driver, for seamless driving. Sometimes, it could take time to make proper adjustment to the mirrors if the vehicle is driven by multiple users. To reduce this discomfort to the driver and to make the vehicle as ‘ready-to-go’ as possible, this feature is developed. The eye position of the driver is calculated, and coarse adjustment of the mirrors are done while also providing the customer an option of fine adjustment since mirror positioning is subjective. The leg position is calculated to define the steering position and seat position.

articleTitle: Smart Thermal System in Electric Vehicle
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for automatically determining battery temperature during vehicle off periods. Subsequently, the proposed system activates the compressor and cooling circuit, or heater and heating circuit based on the prevailing environmental conditions. Battery temperatures are retrieved from the Battery Management System at regular intervals (proposed interval: every 4 hours when the vehicle is off). The Master controller continuously monitors temperature data and triggers the compressor or heater when temperatures exceed or fall below predefined threshold values, established through calibration and considering the maximum and minimum temperature range. Furthermore, the optimal temperature profile, derived from extensive calibration, can be applied to all weather conditions, ensuring maximum battery life.

articleTitle: Linearization of Over-Modulation Region for a Dodecagonal Space Vector Structure with a Single DC Source
abstract: The main advantage of dodecagonal space vector pulse width modulation (PWM) scheme for open-end winding induction motor (OEWIM) drives includes the elimination of the fifth and seventh harmonics and suppression of eleventh and thirteenth harmonics in the motor phase voltages. However, this scheme requires two isolated DC sources or a single DC source and a capacitor with a voltage controller. In this paper, a dodecagonal space vector PWM method is proposed for a dodecagonal space vector connected with a single DC source and a capacitor fed inverter without any voltage controller, thus simplifying the circuit to a large extent. The voltage across the capacitor of the second inverter will be maintained constant without any controller using the proposed modulation method. Also, to utilize the DC source to its maximum limit and to improve the speed range of induction motor, a modulation scheme is implemented to linearize the over-modulation region. Also, there is a smooth transition from one linear region through over-modulation region to 12-step mode using the proposed modulation method. Experimental results are included to verify the proposed modulation method.

articleTitle: Experimental and Numerical Studies on Battery Temperature Distribution
abstract: Accurate temperature measurement and thermal management of lithium-ion batteries are of utmost importance nowadays because of their significant influence on battery performance, cycle life, battery degradation, safety etc. But measurement of battery core temperatures on electric vehicles in real time is a challenge due to the complex design and microstructure of the cell. So, the onboard diagnostic systems measure cell skin temperatures and use correlation algorithms to estimate thermal distribution. But the battery skin temperature does not exactly reflect the battery core temperature and the uncertainties are to be overcome with complex estimation algorithms. In the current work, detailed experimental studies were conducted on M50 21700 cylindrical cell to determine voltage and temperature characteristics with different discharge rates at ambient temperature. Using the test data, a 1-D coupled thermal electrochemical model of cell was built and validated which can predict battery voltage and average cell temperature for different operating conditions. Then a 3D CFD model of the cell is developed using the thermal parameters of the 1D model and the lumped heat generation terms are ported from 1D to 3D using a coupled approach. The 3D model is validated by the comparison of temperature with 1D. From the tests, temperature difference between cell core to outer skin is measured and the temperature gradient is imposed on the 3D model by tuning the thermal parameters. The 3D CFD model when extrapolated into cell and module level helps to analyze the heat transfer and temperature distribution for different coolant flow rate conditions. The developed approach can also help onboard thermal management algorithms to make better estimation of battery temperature which would help in efficient battery cooling and managing safety.

articleTitle: Role of Machine Learning Approach in the Assessment of Lithium-Ion Battery's SOC for EV Application
abstract: To emphasize the safety and accurate state of charge operation of the lithium battery is essential for EVs. In addition, they are increasingly being used in manned and unmanned aerial aircraft, grid-connected load-leveling applications, electric vehicles (EVs), and other fields. Battery deterioration typically follows a non-linear path. Numerous studies have demonstrated that the main causes of battery aging are temperature and the discharge or charge rate. Due to the intricate and usually unclear internal dynamics of lithium-ion batteries, reliable and illustrative strategies are unavailable to estimate the state of health of the battery. It is highly tedious work to predict SOC with substantially less degradation. The paper illustrates the significance and contribution of different machine-learning algorithms in the estimation of the SOC of the battery.

articleTitle: A Switched-Capacitor Based Multilevel Inverter with Extendable Levels having Enhanced Voltage Gain for Renewable Energy Applications
abstract: Various Switched-Capacitor based Multilevel Inverters (SCMLI) are suggested in literature. These converters can, however, provide fixed levels of ac output voltage. A higher number of renewable energy units must be linked in line for the converter to be able to create an extendable ac output voltage. This is because the converter needs switches with high voltage stress and low voltage gains. To fill this gap, an SC-MLI is proposed in this paper to produce 5, 7, 9 and 11-levels in ac output voltage waveform with a voltage gain of 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5, respectively. Instead of altering the converter design, these levels of ac output voltage can only be obtained by changing the switching scheme. The proposed converter includes 12 switches, 2 dc-link capacitors and 2 switched-capacitors units along with one dc voltage source. The proposed configuration also has the advantage of having fewer devices with the capacitor voltage self-balancing and higher efficiency due to greater power loss sharing amongst the switches. Furthermore, auxiliary diodes are not needed for the proposed converter. This feature makes the proposed converter to be used in high efficiency applications. The proposed topology can further be extended for a higher number of levels and higher voltage gain by including cascaded connections of the proposed converter. A one-kW power-rated prototype that was developed in the lab is used to validate the proposed converter's performance.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Right Data Over Big Data for Autonomous Driving using Data Analytics
abstract: Autonomous Driving is becoming increasingly complex, requiring the continuous tuning of different perception models for a variety of road scenarios, from simple to critical. To achieve the best performance, “data” plays a crucial role in every stage of product development, simulation, and validation of models for autonomous vehicles. Is “big data” (petabytes) alone sufficient to attain better performance? Or it is important to find the “right data” for the “right use cases” at the “right time” over “big data”. This paper represents the importance of “data analytics” for autonomous driving where “right data” is more important. In the context of autonomous driving, data analytics can be applied at two levels: active analytics (techniques to collect the right data for the right use cases – more direct and saves cost) and passive analytics (techniques to find the right data among petabytes of collected data – incurs more costs and time).

articleTitle: Single Electric Motor Full Hybrid Solution for Developing Markets
abstract: Hybrid vehicles are a fundamental step towards clean mobility, especially for countries that lack adequate fast charging infrastructure, access to green electricity and battery recycling technology. Full hybrid vehicles are modular and can be offered with or without external charging options. Without external charging, hybrids deliver exceptional fuel economy via regenerative braking and engine efficiency optimization. Adding an external charger extends the pure electric range to cover daily commute without having the range anxiety for longer drives. Within the available concepts, a single electric motor hybrid is the best solution for emerging markets as it can be cost-effective due to high level of localization and deliver comparable level of efficiency to the 2 motor hybrid solutions available in Japanese and European markets.

articleTitle: Handling and Stability Comparison of Three- Wheeled Vehicle With Delta and Tadpole Design
abstract: Throughout the world, three-wheelers have generally lagged traditional four-wheelers in terms of popularity. Three-wheelers with a delta design are frequently used as taxis in India and other developing nations for short- to medium-distance travel. Because of its low cost-to-efficiency ratio, it is also used commercially. Since three-wheelers are more compact than four-wheelers compared to motorcycles, they are typically utilized for personal transportation in developed nations. Three-wheeled vehicles with the Tadpole and Delta configurations can handle quite differently, and each has its own benefits and drawbacks. This study aims to first compare the Tadpole and Delta configurations' static stability factors for both passenger and commercial use. Using Multibody Simulation software, the handling performance of both configurations will be examined. The study will also compare the FWD and RWD Tadpole configuration designs and will be offering design recommendations for vehicles that will alleviate their propensity to roll over.

articleTitle: Accelerating Automotive Design: Harnessing AI Models for Efficient 3D Design and Development of Automobile Systems and Subsystems
abstract: Generative AI has captured the world's attention since its groundbreaking debut in 2021 through the release of Dall-E and propelled innovation into unexplored territories. The 3D automotive models will be transformed eventually, thanks to the AI models which is presented in this work, which blends a text-conditioned diffusion model with a 3D reconstruction model. By leveraging acquired data, our model makes informed assumptions about new designs and specifications, utilizing text prompts as input. Through this process, the diffusion model generates remarkable 2D images, subsequently reconstructed into 3D representations. This study highlights the profound implications and unprecedented efficiency brought forth by AI models in the automotive domain, paving the way for unparalleled advancements and co-development along with human intelligence.

articleTitle: Influence of Different Direct Cooling Systems on Interior Permanent Magnet Traction Machine Performance
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of direct cooling systems on a 3-phase 12 slot/10 pole, 30kW interior permanent magnet machine for electric two-wheeler applications. Both in-slot oil cooling and shaft spray cooling models have been developed, allowing to compare with an air-cooling system in terms of continuous torque-speed envelopes and drive cycle efficiency. Multi-domain simulations have been carried out using Ansys Motor-CAD. It is found that the best continuous performance is obtained by shaft spray cooling and the in-slot oil cooling on its own is the least attractive. The combination of in-slot oil cooling and air cooling shows a significantly better performance than air cooling but the gain in the continuous torque may not justify the design and manufacturing complexity associated with it.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Model for Vehicle Cooling System
abstract: To facilitate wide-spread acceptance of Electric Vehicles (EVs), it is essential to increase their range. One of the ways to achieve this is by reducing the energy consumption for cooling the battery by increasing the efficiency of the cooling strategy using predictive thermal management. Predictive thermal management can be used to switch on the cooling system whenever needed thereby minimizing the energy wastage which can otherwise be used to drive the vehicle. Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with Levenberg-Marquardt Algorithm as optimizer is being employed as the predictor. Initially, the battery output current will be predicted using which the future values of the battery temperature will be predicted. The current predictor has Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2.866 and Coefficient of Correlation (R) of 0.988 while the corresponding values for the temperature predictor are 0.829 and 0.986 respectively.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Based Vehicle to Two Vehicle (V22V) Charging
abstract: Resonant Inductive Coupling (RIC) Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technologies allow for the simultaneous charging of multiple Electric Vehicles (EVs) even as they drive. In such configurations, vehicle receivers often encounter magnetic cross-coupling. This cross-coupling not only complicates receiver control but also significantly diminishes the output power of each receiver. To enhance the output power, this paper presents a compensation method designed to counteract the effects of cross-coupling. Preliminary analysis of the requirements to compensate for cross-coupling indicates that controlling the current phase in each receiver, ensuring it's orthogonal to the phase of the transmitter current, is crucial. This method effectively compensates for the interference brought about by cross-coupling. Magnetic and power transfer simulations for various charging modes are conducted using ANSYS Maxwell and MATLAB/Simulink®, respectively. Experimental validation of the proposed method involves a 2 kW transmitter coil and two 1 kW receiver coils, demonstrating the Vehicle-to-Two-Vehicles (V22V) WPT.

articleTitle: Study On Performance Simulation of 100kW Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell For Heavy Commercial Vehicle Applications
abstract: The integration of fuel cell technology utilizing hydrogen as a fuel holds immense promise for the advancement of heavy-duty commercial vehicle solutions. Presently, a plethora of fuel cell variants cater to diverse vehicle applications. Within this array, the proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) demonstrates remarkable potential for automotive use owing to its attributes of low operating temperature and high power density. However, the direct global implementation of fuel cell technology concepts into the Indian commercial vehicle (CV) market is not feasible. Further, the functional requirements of the fuel cell (FC) system, including the balance of plant (BoP), should be meticulously chosen to ensure optimal FC vehicle performance without performance compromise. Inaddition, PEMFC power supplies are available in various power ratings however, the selection of an optimized fuel cell power configuration for heavy-duty applications proves to be a daunting task due to cost sensitivity and market competitiveness in India. To address this challenges, comprehensive simulation studies are imperative to unravel the performance dynamics of PEMFC under varying vehicle operating conditions. In this study, a simulation model of a Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle (FCEV) truck with a load range exceeding 20–40 tons is developed utilizing GT-SUITE software. Based on a thorough investigation of steady state and transient simulation performances, a 100-kW FC system is identified as the optimal power configuration for the specified vehicle tonnage.

articleTitle: General Electric Testing: Simulate and Test – Possible Failures of Vehicle Electric System
abstract: General Electric (GE) tests are based on core Electrical and Electronics (E&E) design principles. With technology advancements in automotive domain, it seems like the core of E&E engineering practices are taken casually, with an abstraction that everything will work well. However, this technology advancements had made consideration of core engineering practices more crucial in design; otherwise, chances of this advancement getting failed at initial stages of vehicle integration is more. This document is going to cover core of E&E practices for GE tests. Going forward, we will discuss different GE test cases, their importance and design considerations.

articleTitle: Small Signal Analysis and Control of High Speed PMSM Drive Consisting of LCL Filter
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM), having fundamental frequency (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{1}$</tex>) more than 500 Hz, are gaining popularity in high-speed application due to compactness in size and reduced losses. Size constraints demand better thermal management and reduction in harmonic & core losses in the motor. Further, high dv/dt of PWM voltage causes leakage currents in bearing and impacts the insulation as well. Therefore, such drives need nearly sinusoidal input voltage at the motor terminals. LCL filter-based drives improve the input power quality. However, these are inherently unstable, and suitable damping is required to stabilize the drive. This paper analyzes the LCL filter-based drive through small signal analysis. The pole-zero plot on complex s-plane of PMSM drive with and without LCL filter are plotted to identify the instability zones. Based on analysis, a suitable damping factor is proposed to stabilize the drive over complete range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{1}$</tex>. LCL filter-based three-phase PMSM drive, rated at 916 Hz and 50 kW, is used for simulation. Active damping with the proposed damping factor is implemented to validate the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: A Review on Electric Vehicle Battery Modeling Methods
abstract: The battery model is an indispensable tool for the design of battery-powered systems. Battery modeling defines battery behavior analysis, battery condition monitoring, the real-time controller's design, fault diagnosis, and thermal management. Battery modeling is an important part of enhancing the battery development process and monitoring the behavior of battery systems. In addition, electric vehicle battery modeling is necessary for safe charging and discharging along with optimized battery consumption. This study provides a detailed review of various battery modeling methodologies, which include the battery electrical model, the battery thermal model, and the battery coupled model. The comparison of different battery modeling methods is carried out to define the most accurate and reliable battery model for the application of electric vehicle battery management systems and their applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Decarbonization Policies on Electric Vehicle Integration and Carbon Emission: A Singapore Case Study
abstract: This paper examines the potential impact of decarbonization policies of Singapore on electric vehicles (EV) integration and carbon emission. The study focuses on understanding the key drivers, challenges, and opportunities associated with the integration of EVs into Singapore's transportation system and evaluates their potential contribution in reducing greenhouse gas emissions when coupled with different decarbonatization policies. As Singapore confronts unique challenges in reducing emissions, the study explores three energy trends: Clean Energy Renaissance (CER), Climate Action Bloc (CAB), and Emergent Technology Trailblazer (ETT). Using an open-source Energy Transition Model, the research analyzes various factors such as EV adoption rates, energy demand implications, supply technologies and policy frameworks on grid development to assess the impact of EV penetration on carbon emission. Results shows that the transport sector emission in 2050 drops by 43.75% due to the full electrification of the land vehicle population. The CAB energy policy which performed best among the three energy trends with a 62.8% reduction in carbon emission from 2019 level is unable to achieve net zero even with full transport electrification. Therefore, a system's perspective is important in net zero policy development as both clean electricity production and electric vehicle integration are intertwined. With these insights, Singapore can strategically integrate EVs into its decarbonization journey, fostering a sustainable, low-carbon future while mitigating climate change impacts.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Lithium-Ion Battery Recovery Strategy on e-Mobility Revolution
abstract: Better performance characteristics make lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) a favourable power source for electric vehicles (EVs). An increasing share of electro-mobility in the transportation sector increases LIBs demand, generating a large pool of end-of-life (EOL) LIBs when LIBs capacity reaches 80% of their nominal capacity. Therefore, proper EOL LIB management techniques are required to handle the EOL LIB stock. This research systematically uses system dynamics modelling to analyse the trade-offs between LIB recycling and LIB second-use by varying LIB electrode composition, collection rate and capacity of the recovery process. Our study shows that incrementing the collection rate (from 30% to 70%) will reduce landfills and increase the quantity of recovered strategic raw materials, Nickel, by 138%. Model results indicate that technological advancement in LIB electrode chemical composition will increase Nickel recovery, whereas Cobalt recovery is reduced with technological improvement of LIB electrodes.

articleTitle: Coupled Inductor Based SIDO-Buck Converter with Self-Adaptive Digital PWM Control for 12V/24V On-Board Lighting and Dashboard System for 48V-EV
abstract: This paper analyses the CI-SIDO based Buck converter for continuous current with regulated rated voltage for lighting loads and dashboard sensors for an on-board EV system. In the existing lighting unit, individual parallel converters at board level faces the problem of individual conversion, footprint space occupancy and inefficient stability. The proposed CI-SIDO Buck converter is designed for the rating of 12V with a capability of 75Watts and 24V with a capability of 125 Watts providing a line of voltage to multiple loads of 12V and 24V range. The converter under consideration is controlled by a digital PWM with an upgraded control logic of self-adaptive discrete PI controller. The adoption of self-adaptive PI controller helps in addressing the cross-regulation problem, which is more common in multiple output converters. The proposed design is employed for several R-loads on 12V and 24V, mimicking the presence of EV lights, dashboard sensor unit, warm conditioning pumps, air conditioning pumps, and other electronic appliances inside the communication and infotainment units. The CI-SIDO Buck converter with self-adaptive PI controllers is simulated using Matlab-Simscape platform and the same has been implemented in hardware with 16-Bit digital signal processor TMS570LC4357 TI unit.

Author Keywords: Coupled Inductor and SIDO buck converter

articleTitle: Enhancement of Misalignment Tolerance in Multi-Transmitter Wireless Electric Vehicle Charging System Through an Optimal Transmitter Stimulation
abstract: In wireless power Transfer (WPT) based Electric vehicle (EV) charging system the efficiency of power transfer gets reduced due to misalignment between transmitter and receiver coil. Multi-transmitter coil approach instead of single transmitter can improve the misalignment tolerance. This paper presents four transmitter coils with a single receiver coil to improve the misalignment tolerance with optimal stimulation. Instead of stimulating all four transmitter coils, only one transmitter coil is stimulated, whichever is almost or exactly aligned to the receiver coil. Based on the current distribution over, all the Tx coils the optimal Tx coil is identified without using additional sensors on the Rx side. The Tx coils' current distribution is calculated theoretically using mutual inductance obtained from ANSYS-Maxwell simulation of the coil geometry. Using these current distribution data, the corresponding transmitter coil is stimulated optimally, improving the transfer efficiency even with 50 percent misalignment.

articleTitle: North West America Mackenzie Valley Wolf Population Updating during Hunting Inspired Optimization and Quasi-Opposition Based Indian Leopard Cat Swarm Algorithm for Real Power Loss Diminution in Electrical Grid Transmission System for Smart City
abstract: In this paper North West America Mackenzie Valley Wolf Population Updating during Hunting Inspired Optimization (NWPO) Algorithm and Quasi-Opposition based Indian Leopard Cat Swarm (QILC) Algorithm are applied for Real Power Loss Diminution in Electrical Grid Transmission System for Smart City. In NWPO the calculated values for the objective function are an appropriate standard for examining the excellence of the elucidations through examination agents. The preeminent rate which has been computed for the objective function relates to the finest examination agent. Variances in the locations of the examination agents and the sign of variance of the binary standards are utilized. In QILC, initial Indian Leopard Cat population is created and each Indian Leopard Cat represents a solution. In the created population one cluster will monitor the environments and another cluster will passage towards the prey. The time period taken by the Indian Leopard Cat in the movement segment towards the prey is little and accordingly the clusters are defined. In the quest segment mode Indian Leopard Cat will monitor the surroundings. Passages of Indian Leopard Cat will be happened, only when a prey identified or it senses some threat. Projected NWPO and QILC validated in IEEE 57, 300 and 220 KV Grid systems. Real Power loss diminution, deviance and stability expansion attained.

Author Keywords: North West America Mackenzie Valley Wolf

articleTitle: IoT based Electric Vehicle Battery Parameters Monitoring for Battery Swapping
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) is the most widely impacting technology in the immediate future in road transportation. The EVs at the charging station have to wait for a significant amount of time for their recharge. For the solution of this, EV battery parameters are monitored and Batteries swapped in the upcoming charging station. In this regards the battery parameters are monitored; the EV battery is connected to the server for monitoring the health of the battery and the corresponding parameters are stored in the server. The server notifies to the driver about the upcoming charging station, mileage limits and the battery condition. The proposed work discusses the battery parameters required for swapping like state of charge (SOC), State of Health (SOH), and temperature estimated. This research work is implemented in real time EV using an Internet of Things (IoT). The real-time EV parameters are monitored through IoT stored in the cloud.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Optimization of an Outer Rotor-Five Phase Switched Reluctance Motor for In-Wheel Drive Applications
abstract: This article present a design methodology and optimization of a 20/16 outer rotor-five-phase switched reluctance motor (OR-FPSRM) for in-wheel drive applications. The analytical model to estimate the static torque for the OR-FPSRM has been derived. The proposed model depends solely on the geometry parameters, making it highly suitable for design optimization. The motor design process includes mathematical modeling, optimization, CAD modeling, and finite element analysis. The genetic algorithm for optimization has been used, considering the stator pole arc angle, phase current, number of turns, bore diameter, and stack length as optimization variables. The torque density and copper losses serve as objective functions governing the optimization. The optimized motor model is analyzed using ANSYS Maxwell. Comparison results between static finite element analysis solutions and the derived analytical model are presented. Additionally, presented results for performance parameters such as torque, speed, and current waveform.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Input Based EV Charging System with Multi -Mode Power Flow and Adaptive Optimal Power Management Scheme
abstract: In this paper, a renewable energy source (RES) rein-forced grid-integrated electric vehicle (EV) charging system with an adaptive optimal power management (AOPM) scheme has been proposed. The system offers multi-mode bidirectional power flow i.e. grid-to-vehicle (G2V), RES-to-grid (PV2G), renewable energy storage system (RESS)-to-grid (RESS2G), vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) etc. with seamless transition. The AOPM scheme administrates all the operation depending upon the available source, load demand, couple, and decouple the sub-system to ensure no power wastage, maximum utilization of the RES, and reduced grid tariff thus optimizing the power utilization. The operation of the proposed scheme is divided into various modes and the scheme guarantees a seamless transit between these modes without disrupting the battery charging operation and power quality. Additionally, it automatically places the various source-side converters in standby mode, adapting to various worst-case scenarios effectively. An experimental prototype of a 10 kW peak has been developed to verify the proposed system with the AOPM scheme.

articleTitle: Mechanical Integrity Simulation of Sense-Lines in High Voltage Battery Module Used in Battery Electric Vehicle
abstract: This paper introduces computational method to maintain structural integrity of sense-lines used in Lithium Ion (Li-Ion) batteries in Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV). Sense-lines are primary sensing elements of any High Voltage (HV) battery pack to understand the thermal and electrical conditions and hence requires complete protection against various mechanical loads such as mechanical shock, vibration, and thermal loads. In this paper, explicit structural simulation code is used to monitor forces going through the sensing component and ensure no failure of the joint or the component itself during mechanical shock accelerations. The study involves examining different modeling approaches and propose a technique which is simplified and provide accurate failure responses. Validation of proposed modeling is performed using fixture level testing at module level and correlating the structural accelerations at various locations within the battery module. Coupon level testing of sense-lines aids in developing the target for each design and can be leveraged even for early-stage development and validation of the designs.

articleTitle: System Validation with Battery-in-the-Loop Configuration Using a Virtual Testing Toolchain
abstract: Today, the battery development process for automotive applications is relatively decoupled from the vehicle integration and system design validation phase. Battery module design targets are often disregarded at very early design phases even though they are thoroughly linked to the vehicle-level requirements such as performance, lifetime, and cost. Here, AVL proposes a methodology guided by virtual testing techniques to consider vehicle-level validation steps in a very early phase of battery testing. This paper focuses on the benefits of the methodology for both battery suppliers and automotive OEMs. Applications based on a modular virtual testing toolchain which involves a simulation platform and numerous models are comprehensively explained, as well as the generation of the model parameters and the test cases.

articleTitle: Powering the Future: Harnessing an Ecosystem Approach to Drive Electric Vehicle Adoption
abstract: India is expected to witness record growth in electric vehicle (EV) sales to be able to achieve the pledged targets of 30% sales from EVs in 2030. A well-coordinated ecosystem is necessary for a holistic and sustainable growth of the sector. The article discusses the challenges associated with the high adoption of EVs, and the role of the EV ecosystem in unlocking them. Aggressive and integrated approaches are required to support this rapid shift. A holistic approach is taken to identify the interconnections and interdependencies to enable clean energy integration, managed charging, parking regulations, battery safety and standards, battery re-use and recycling, etc. By adopting such an ecosystem approach India will be able to unlock the full potential of EVs to achieve our long-term climate change and energy targets.

articleTitle: Virtual Road Load Data Acquisition using MATLAB for Gearboxes
abstract: RLDA (Road Load Data Acquisition) is a process of acquiring load response of subject vehicles against actual driving conditions on test tracks or actual roads. Vehicle response parameters such as engine torque, engine speed, gear position, wheel torque etc. are measured during this acquisition. The acquired data is processed to derive duty cycles for component level validation on test benches and provides important information about the behavior of subject vehicles to further optimize components. RLDA can only be done on prototype vehicles or a similar vehicle available in market. RLDA requires specific instruments for acquisition of data. There is always a possibility of any failure of the recording equipment or sensor or component of prototype vehicle during measurement, which will affect the complete activity, project timeline and accuracy of measurement. The paper proposes a methodology to conduct RLDA virtually for powertrain using tool developed in MATLAB. Vehicle parameters, driveline component details, drive cycles etc. will be used as an input to derive time series data. This data is further converted to distance domain for derivation of the duty cycle for the powertrain components. The simulated duty cycle generated using the proposed tool show good amount of correlation with duty cycle derived by physical measurements on intended vehicle.

articleTitle: Low Distortion Multilevel Inverter for Efficient Solar PV Generation for EV Application
abstract: Renewable power generation has zero carbon emissions in various cases, but due to their default generation mode (DC power, such as in solar PV, fuel cells, etc.), these require inverters to supply the power to the ac loads. The power quality is an issue to address while doing DC/AC inversion and is also important for key EV applications such as driving EV motor. The inverters required may be of conventional 3-level, multi-pulse, or multi-level types. For the integration of discrete dc sources (such as SPV, fuel cell, etc.), multi-level inverters (MLIs) are preferred due to the various advantages of this structure. For the operation of MLIs, different modulation techniques are available in the literature viz. fundamental frequency switching or high-frequency switching. Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in the output voltage produced by the inverter depends on the switching scheme chosen. To meet the requirement of various standards on harmonics, in this work, an optimized Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (SHE-PWM) technique is implemented for the control of a 9-level MLI. The proposed scheme improves the productivity of the inverter system as compared to Sinusoidal PWM (SPWM). In the presented scheme, THD due to odd harmonic components (including triplen harmonics) up to 49<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order has been minimized using Genetic Algorithm Optimization (GAO) technique by considering multiple transitions per quarter cycle. It has been observed that the THD and distinct harmonic components up to the 49<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order are within the limit set by various standards on harmonics. The viability of the presented scheme has been tested using analytical and simulation studies on a 9-level MLI.

articleTitle: Energy efficient Onboard EV Charger Employing Partial Power Processing DC-DC Converter
abstract: This paper presents the two configurations of partial power processing converter for onboard electric vehicles (EVs) charging using the traditional full power processing dual active bridge DC-DC converter. The two configurations are Input Parallel and Output Series (IPOS) Series Output Parallel (ISOP) partial power converters for high- and low-voltage battery charging applications. IPOS and ISOP can bidirectional power transfer from source to battery and vice-versa through the direct and partial paths. The partial path only comprises passive and magnetic components, whereas no components are on the direct path. To validate the performance of the proposed configurations of partial power processing, converters have been simulated and tested using MATLAB / Simulink toolbox, and their results are compared with the full-power processing dual active bridge converter under the various loaded conditions. The results show that the IPOS and ISOP configurations provide an efficiency of about 94% under full load conditions, i.e., during battery charging and observed to be 4–6% higher than the full power converter configuration. Also, IPOS and ISOP schemes handle less than 50% of output power via the partial paths. Therefore, power ratings and sizes of the semiconductor and passive devices can be significantly reduced compared to the full power converter. Hence, it is observed that these two configurations are best suited for onboard EV chargers.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Quality Issues in Fast Charging Stations on a Real-Time Simulator
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are becoming sustainable alternatives in the transportation sector. The shift towards electric mobility increases the requirement for suitable charging infrastructure. The charging speed depends on the electrical capacity of the charging infrastructure and not solely on the charging station. Large-scale penetration of EVs requires a steady rapid charging infrastructure for EVs. The impact of fast charging stations (FCS) on the utility grid is severe owing to the presence of semiconductor devices. The power quality issues affected to a larger extent due to FCS are voltage profile, harmonics, and transformer overloading. This paper presents the analysis of these power quality issues with the FCS developed according to the guidelines of the Government of India EV Policy using the framework of MATLAB/Simulink. Moreover, the simulation results acquired from the developed FCS are substantiated using real-time experiments on a Hardware-In-Loop (HIL) real-time simulator, OPAL-RT OP4510.

articleTitle: A Multifunction Multioutput On-board Power Processor for Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper proposes a multifunction multioutput on-board power processor (MMPP) for electric vehicles (EVs). The proposed on-board power processor can charge the battery with any available source (AC or DC) at charging port or through any other available EV during vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) charging operation. In V2V charging operation, two EVs can quickly exchange the required amount of energy with each other. Further, while AC charging, the unity power factor is maintained at the source terminal. In all the charging method the constant-current and constant-voltage (CC-CV) is maintained at the battery terminal. In the proposed MMPP, the requirement of an additional speed-control converter and auxiliary battery for cabin power demand is eliminated by using a HIGH-PWM-LOW-ON switching scheme and multioutput operation of the proposed system respectively. The effectiveness of the proposed MMPP is experimentally validated with 320 W prototype for charging operation and with 550 W prototype for motoring operation.

articleTitle: A Non-Linear Voltage Controller for Grid Voltage Sensor-Less Power Factor Correction Converters
abstract: In this paper, a grid voltage sensor-less control scheme for an AC-DC power factor correction converter using a non-linear voltage controller is proposed. The conventional PFC converters, used in EV battery chargers, electric drive systems, and computer power supplies, require a grid voltage sensor in order to operate at unity power factor. By using the proposed non-linear control method, the grid voltage sensor, and Phase Locked Loop (PLL) are not required for unity power factor operation of the PFC converter. The proposed grid voltage sensor-less control scheme also provides an additional degree of freedom (a), for controlling the transient response of the converter and its effect on the same in terms of peak overshoot and settling time for DC-link voltage is reviewed and analyzed. The mathematical equation for the grid current drawn by a PFC converter using the proposed control scheme is also derived and using it, the effect of circuit parameters on the power factor of the converter can be predicted. With the proposed control scheme, the system's overall cost, size, and weight are reduced, making it more reliable, less complex, and cost-effective. The proposed control scheme is simulated in MATLAB-Simulink for steady-state and transient conditions, and some hardware experiment results are also included.

articleTitle: A Dual Receiver and Inherent CC-CV Operated WRIPT EV Charging System with High Misalignment Tolerance Couplers
abstract: This article proposes a dual receiver and inherent automatic CC-CV charging, features-based Wireless Resonant Inductive Power Transfer (WRIPT) EV charging system for high misalignment tolerance couplers. For the dual receiver with high misalignment tolerance coupling; two square coils are used on the Receiver (Rx) side and a Double ‘D’ (DD) coil is used on the Transmitter (Tx) side. In an actual working environment, the coupler architecture undergoes various possible misalignments and some rare possible misalignments, which affect the Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) of the WRIPT EV charging system. This investigation deals by considering parameters for comparative analysis of the possible misalignments are; airgap distance, coupling factor, Self-inductance of the Tx and Rx coils, and Mutual inductance, concerning possible misalignment parameters. Then, by considering the load variations, dependencies of coupling architecture, and resonant frequency of the WRIPT system, it is important to provide the battery charging with the desired CC-CV charging mode. Hence, the inherent CC-CV output characteristics of resonant compensator with dual receiver coil are developed in the secondary onboard system for the 3.3 kW power capacity prototype. The CC followed by CV output mode can be achieved for battery charging with high misalignment tolerance without the need for an extra DC-DC chopper and its complicated control strategy. By supplying fixed control frequency Zero-Phase Angle (ZPA) condition and Zero-Voltage Switching (ZVS) soft switching was achieved.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Various PWM Strategies for Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines in High Voltage EV Application
abstract: An efficient control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is required for a high-performance electric drive. The type of modulation technique used to switch the Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) is essential to achieve higher DC bus utilization, lower the switching losses and harmonics, and improve the system efficiency. Space Vector PWM (SVPWM) and Third Harmonic Injected PWM (THIPWM) are two such modulation techniques for inverter switching. A detailed performance analysis is presented in this paper considering these two modulation techniques in the flux weakening area of operation for given load profile. A modified average power switching loss calculation model is developed to calculate the power loss during the hard switching of the IGBTs. A detailed comparison of IGBT power loss is presented with the comparison of average power calculation method and the modified power loss calculation model adapted for three-phase VSI. The Total Harmonic Distortion analysis (THD) uses the Fast Fourier Transformation analysis (FFT) tool. The entire system modeling and simulation were done using MATLAB/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Adopting Security and Privacy Risk-Based Engineering in Designing and Handling AI/ML Based Applications for Road Vehicles
abstract: In the recent decade, advancements and innovations in the automotive industries have mostly been driven by machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). Vehicle software features are designed and engineered out of the data collected from various sources, such as sensors, actuators, cameras, roadside infrastructure, radar, lidar, and sometimes the supplier's or original equipment manufacturer's specific servers. But data poisoning, privacy violations, unintended behaviors, vulnerabilities, compromising cybersecurity goals, and model theft are also growing exponentially in AI and ML systems. As the automotive industry is a regulation- and quality-driven industry, can AI/ML-based features be assessed with reference to security and privacy risks? In this paper, the author would like to propose a novel approach to managing AI and ML applications by providing the preconditions, checklist, and RASIC resulting from attacking AI and ML models, technology gap analysis with a case study of ADAS algorithms, and risk assessment. Most importantly, thinking like an attacker means fooling one's own model into acting adversely.

Author Keywords: defense in depth and differential Privacy

articleTitle: Financial Impact on Indian Automotive Industry for Transition from IC Engine Based to EV Based Technology
abstract: The transition from IC Engine to EV Technology is expected will effect financially and non-financially both. On one side, the transition from IC engine vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs) technology is expected to impact the automotive industry and the government financially, and on the other side, it is also likely to impact the end user significantly. This study aims to analyze the financial impact of the transition on the mobility on India. For this, it takes into account the different aspects including production overhaul, technology transfer, government policy, skilling, employability, other associated aspects on Indian economy in accordance with GoI's EV 30@30 policy. The initial findings of the study involves financial calculations and and infers that the transition could cost about INR 13 Lakh Crore. However, the transition also brings a positive hope for the coming generation. The study shall first examine the cost of overall transition and then critically analyze whether the expenditure is justified or not.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study of Utilizing Directly Recycled LiFePO4 Cathodes for Second Life Usage in Stationary Applications
abstract: The exponential growth of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) leads to a rise in the number of spent LIBs and causes environmental and global sustainability issues. Recycling is one of the methods to address these issues. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of using low-cost, recycled black mass lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material (LFP R) in combination with new virgin LFP cathode material (LFP V) for second-life usage in coin cell LIB batteries. Five different compositions of spent LFPs and virgin LFPs were tested, and the results showed that the LFP 5050 composition exhibited the optimum performance in terms of cyclic stability, with 90 percent capacity retention at 50 percent of the cost of virgin LFP for up to 300 cycles. The study suggests that direct physical mixing of recycled LFP cathode material with new virgin LFP cathode material is better suited for secondary storage applications, such as stationary storage and powering electronic devices, than primary applications, such as electric vehicles. These results will have a big impact on how cost-effective and sustainably LIB batteries could be produced in the future.

articleTitle: Electro-thermal Model using Advanced ECM Approach for Automotive Application
abstract: The burgeoning demand for electric vehicles (EVs) necessitates comprehensive electro-thermal modeling of Li-ion batteries. This study presents Advanced Equivalent Circuit Modeling (AECM) approach to create a precise electro-thermal model for Li-ion cells. The main goal is to provide reliable inputs for assessing vehicle performance and optimizing battery thermal management systems. Using a Design of Experiments approach, critical parameters like cell capacity, RC parameters, faradic efficiency, entropic coefficients, and specific heat capacity are derived. Tests like hybrid-pulse power characterization, capacity, and open circuit voltage are tailored to mimic real-world usage scenarios. The resulting models accurately predict voltage response, cell temperatures, and reversible/irreversible heat generation, validated against real-world data. Notably, these models predict heat and temperature across a wide range (-10°C to 60°C) and loading conditions, making them valuable for hardwarein-the-loop (HIL), software-in-the-loop (SIL), and model-in-theloop (MIL) simulations during EV development. Additionally, these models support test matrix design, failure mode analysis, and battery performance strategies. Limitations include challenges in predicting cell dynamics, particularly at lower state-of-charge (SOC) levels. Future work will integrate an aging model to enhance the models' utility. In conclusion, this research offers a robust electro-thermal model to improve Li-ion battery reliability and performance in electric vehicles, aligning with the growing demand for sustainable transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Scalable Multi-physics Simulation to Support PEM Fuel Cell System Development
abstract: Hydrogen powered fuel cell systems are a promising technology for future CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> neutral vehicle propulsion. In the development of modern fuel cell systems for mobile applications, system simulation is used for a wide variety of tasks, ranging from concept layout to component design to virtual component integration and calibration. An efficient use of simulation requires scalable and consistent models, covering both the variety of application areas and the width of the modeling tasks related to cell, stack, system and vehicle. This article presents a holistic approach to PEM fuel cell system modelling as an enabler for the simulation-supported development of future mobility and transport solutions. The adopted multi-physical system simulation platform offers scalable modeling depth, applicable to fuel cell balance-of-plant development as well as virtual system integration and optimization. The detailed component models for stack and auxiliary units, such as humidifier, injector/ejector, air compressor and water separator, are based on the essential thermodynamic and electrochemical fundamentals. This approach ensures high accuracy and true extrapolation capabilities within the entire relevant system operation parameter space. Numerical robustness and fast solvers enable unconditional real-time capabilities as a prerequisite for efficient use in MiL, SiL and HiL environments. The applicability of the multi-physical simulation framework to fuel cell development related engineering challenges is demonstrated based on selected use-cases regarding humidifier sizing and compressor matching as well as cold-start strategy assessment, performance degradation analysis and control system development.

articleTitle: Design and Development of PSA System for Ultra Purification of Green Hydrogen
abstract: To ensure high-purity standards for Hydrogen used in fuel cell vehicles, the widely employed method of Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) effectively removes impurities from Hydrogen streams. This paper focuses on the design of a PSA cycle for Hydrogen purification using a system consisting of two beds packed with 4Å Molecular Sieve. The Hydrogen feed stream considered in this study contains water, the primary impurity resulting from the electrolysis process. The design of a PSA system involves three crucial steps to achieve optimal performance and efficiency. Firstly, the selection of the adsorbent material and particle size is based on factors like selectivity, capacity, and regenerative ability. Secondly, the superficial velocity of the gas flowing through the bed is determined, considering aspects such as mass transfer kinetics and pressure drop limitations. Finally, the bed length is chosen, considering factors such as desired efficiency, breakthrough time, and bed capacity. The model's results are compared with industrial data obtained from an Oxygen PSA system to validate their accuracy. Deviations from the industrial values may arise due to differences in adsorbent usage, superficial velocity, packing density of the adsorbent, assumptions of adiabatic and ideal gas behaviour, and unknown operating conditions. In the present case, the pressure drop across the bed is assumed to be zero. By applying the PSA design principles and evaluating the model's outputs, this study aims to contribute to the advancement of Hydrogen purification for fuel cell vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Single Pedal Braking on Braking Performance of Electrified Heavy Road Vehicle for Urban Applications
abstract: Electric heavy commercial road vehicles use a regenerative brake system that acts on pressing of brake pedals and co-operates with friction brakes to provide the necessary deceleration. The strategy of applying regenerative braking during accelerator pedal release and its control using accelerator pedal position in the dead zone is focused in this work. It is observed that implementation of this strategy in heavy road vehicles used for urban drive applications has the advantage that under most of the driving conditions, the deceleration requirement is within 0.15 m/s2 and only pure regenerative braking provided with accelerator pedal release is sufficient. This strategy combined with the use of braking by pressing the brake pedal can meet the entire range of deceleration requirements of a vehicle. The results show that higher amount of energy recovery and driving comfort can be achieved with this feature. Further, this strategy is integrated with the complete VCU model and the analysis of different methods of applying regeneration torque viz. constant torque, increasing torque at different rates etc., amount of dead zone to be provided in accelerator pedal and their effect on vehicle speed, deceleration and energy recovery are studied.

articleTitle: Single-Particle model with thermal and electrolyte dynamics for lithium-Ion cell
abstract: The single-particle model, originally presented by Meng Guo [Electrochemical Society, 158 (2) A122-A132 (2011)], is extended to incorporate the effects of temperature and solution phase potential with electrolyte. In this extended model, the simplified nonlinear resistance of the solution phase is replaced by ohmic resistance, neglecting the electric resistance of the connector and the conductivity of the electrode in the solid phase. This replacement is achieved by expressing the resistance as a function of the geometrical parameters of the electrode, along with the effective conductivity of the electrolyte. The electrode overpotential is expressed as the combined sum of kinetic and diffusion overpotentials at both electrodes, disregarding the migration of lithium ions within each electrode's solid phase. The cell model estimates the terminal voltage and cell temperature during galvanostatic operation. The results of existing model taken as benchmark data. The results of the single-particle model for LiCoO2 exhibit an exceptionally good agreement with benchmark voltage data obtained from different discharge profiles (C/33, C/2, and C) and at different starting temperatures (15, 25, 35, and 45°C) of the cell.

articleTitle: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Renewable Energy (RE) Technologies for Grid Peak Load Management and Sustainability: A State-of-the-Art Survey
abstract: Accelerating the e-mobility and renewable energy (RE) revolution to green the global transportation and electricity sectors is undeniably paramount in order to foster sustainable economic progress, safeguard the planet from the perils of climate degradation, mitigate the depletion of fossil fuel resources, and combat the escalating threat of global warming. Therefore, the transportation sector is swiftly shifting from traditional petrol/diesel engine vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs). Similarly, the electricity sector is also rapidly transitioning from fossil-fuel-sourced generation to renewableenergy-sourced generation. These global vicissitudes also ensure oil independence and energy security. The widespread adoption of plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) presents the utility smart electricity grid with great advantages and significant challenges to its techno-economic-sustainable operation. The uncoordinated charging patterns of large-scale PEVs necessitate the drawing of large charging power from the utility smart grid. This leads to an increase in grid peak load and system power losses, operation costs, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, etc. The implementation of Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology efficiently addresses these adverse impacts through smart charging and discharging of PEVs. This paper provides a state-of-the-art survey of current research studies that focus on the implementation of V2G and renewable energy (RE) technologies as effective strategies for grid peak load management and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction providing techno-economic-sustainability in utility smart grid operation. A concise overview of the V2G notion and technology, the impacts of V2G technology, and the optimization of V2G scheduling for PEVs are also given, in addition to research gaps and future recommendations.

articleTitle: Study on Optimization of Ultrasonic Welding Process Parameters of Al-Cu Bimetallic Busbar for use in Battery Electric Vehicle (EV)
abstract: The battery is the power source of an Electric Vehicle (EV) and improving its operational efficiency is one of the requirements to achieve the required product performance and quality. There are numerous electrical connections in the assembly of a battery pack from cell to module and further module to the battery pack. These connections such as Tab-toTab (i.e., cell-to-cell joining to connect the battery cells in series or parallel) and Tab-to-Busbars can be made through various methods such as soldering, crimping, resistance welding, fusion welding, etc. Still, all these conventional joining methods have some mechanical, metallurgical, electrical, and economic constraints that limit the overall process efficiency. One of the factors includes poor weld quality, voids, cracks, pores, and other defects in the weld zone that affect the battery performance. The Ultrasonic Welding (UW) technique can overcome many issues that persist in conventional methods. In this work, we describe the study of the UW zone's mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties based on the mechanical and microstructural analysis using design and validation processes such as lap shear strength tests, Optical Microscopy (OM), and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). Here we attempted the Ultrasonic Welding of Copper and Aluminum of different thicknesses. The thickness of the intermetallic layer in the heataffected zone could be observed with the help of SEM. A 3D thermomechanical model was also developed with ABAQUS to investigate the coupled mechanical and thermal behavior of materials in ultrasonic welding. Results were validated with experimental results, which can be employed to analyze battery pack performance. This study provides important insight into Al and Cu UW for electric vehicle battery assembly as a basis for future research directions in the field.

articleTitle: Development of Wire Bonding as a Joining Technique in Battery Packs
abstract: The automobile industry is switching to electric powered vehicles to minimize carbon (and its oxides) emissions and the amount of air pollution that is brought due to these emissions. A big section of the electric vehicle industry is battery technology. Automotive battery packs consist of a range of battery cells of different form factors that are interconnected in series and parallel connections to shape modules and then connected collectively to form battery pack. These cells are structurally held and electrically connected to each other by means of a joining technique. To enhance the quality, design and to reduce the weight and cost of the battery pack it is very important to choose an appropriate joining technique. These techniques could be spot welding, laser welding, nut / bolt joining or ultrasonic wire bonding. The current work offers an overview of applied sciences for battery manufacturing with merits and demerits. Apart from this a Pugh matrix approach was considered to rate the process. A battery pack was designed and fabricated to evaluate the bonding operations and testing. The parameter at which pull off load is achieved and there are no mechanical stresses is determined and is chosen as the optimized bonding parameter. The cycle time can be decreased by 2.48% and the cost to manufacture the battery pack can be reduced by 38.2% by adapting to ultrasonic wire bonding when compared to traditional resistive spot welding.

articleTitle: Carbon Neutrality Approach, Standards, Regulations, Policies & Circular Economy
abstract: Global warming and unpredictable weather patterns have garnered significant attention and anxiety across global forums. The need to mitigate climate change between 1.5℃ (Celsius) to 2℃ and the ways to reverse greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions has been in the making for a decade now with its core structure insisting on carbon neutrality formulated through Conference of Parties (COP26) with accelerated targets across global countries. In terms of Carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, India ranks third next to United States; its CO2 emission are about one-fourth of China which leads global CO2 emission [1]. With a very steady Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and increasing industrial output, India has determined itself to meet its climate action obligation through National Determined Contribution (NDC) and sustainable alternatives in the Energy, transport, and other sectors. Transport decarbonization, reduction of non-fossil fuels in energy sector and replacing sustainable alternative across sectors are at key focus, from urban housing to farming supported through cleaner technology, smart innovation, continuous investment with government collaboration and support. With India's huge market potential across sectors driven by strong consumer strength and talents across industrial growth and consistent GDP's, the growth in sectors can only accelerate leading towards largest economy. The Scope of this journal is to analyze India's carbon neutrality commitments leveraged by circular economy across sectors, its targets, and the proposed plan. It will also assess the effectiveness of government standards, policies, and regulations through the author's eyes, and to summarize, interpret, and conclude that as a country, India's stand towards carbon neutrality short-term and long-term goals by 2030 and 2070 respectively.

articleTitle: Application of Structural Equation Models to Analyse Barriers for Sustainable Adoption of Hydrogen Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles in India
abstract: This article presents a simplified three-pillar framework for assessing sustainability for hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles in India and identifies that large-scale commercial adoption is a key enabler of sustainability. The barriers for large scale adoption are identified, listed and a survey is conducted to gather responses on 10 concern areas namely awareness, policy, range, safety, reliability, infrastructure, cost, waiting time, social status and resale potential with an objective function of adoption. Whilst based on raw survey data, Safety emerged as key concern area, followed by Reliability and Infrastructure, a thorough mathematical modelling and analysis using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) indicated that interactive effects between the constructs are non-negligible and based on that infrastructure is a key influencing factor on adoption followed by cost. The survey also indicates an emerging trend towards adoption without the need for ownership through rental or lease service.

articleTitle: A Systematic Approach to Mitigate Semiconductor Chip Shortage: Insights and Solutions for the Future Automotive Industry
abstract: Post pandemic world is experiencing fast adoption of technologies like 5G, Internet Of Things, Cloud computing, Electric Vehicle and Artificial Intelligence based tools for improving human quality of life. At the heart of all latest technology is semiconductor chips-based computing. Semiconductors play a crucial role in expediting society's shift towards more sustainable and intelligent systems. The authors emphasize the importance of creating a resilient and flexible supply chain that can withstand disruptions and adapt to changing circumstances. The paper highlights the need for collaboration between industry players, government bodies, and other stakeholders to create a sustainable and efficient supply chain that can meet the growing demand for semiconductor chips in the automotive industry. The paper concludes with a call to action for industry players to promote transparency, standardization, and technological advancement to address the chip shortage and ensure a sustainable future for the automotive industry.

articleTitle: 3-D CFD Simulation of Oil Flow and Heat Transfer in an Electric Drive Unit
abstract: The Electric Drive Unit (EDU) for electric vehicles has high power density and unavoidably generates considerable waste heat during its operation. Thermal management of the Electric Drive Unit is crucial for its reliable, optimum operation. This demands efficient cooling technology. Computation Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation as a virtual test bed, provides detailed insights into the flow, and temperature fields which help in making the necessary design changes for better thermal performance of Electric Drive Unit at the product development phase. The present work deals with the prediction of temperature of the windings during the warming up cycle using a fast and novel coupled heat transfer approach. A 3-D, quasi-steady state, and transient, multiphase flow with conjugate heat transfer model of Electric Drive Unit is simulated in Simerics-MP+, a CFD software. The 3-D model of the drive unit consists of an e-motor with all the primary parts such as windings, end rings, stator, rotor laminate, shaft, and transmission gears. The oil distribution inside the motor is predicted using an explicit Volume of Fluid (VOF) formulation for multiphase flow with high resolution interface capturing between oil and air phases for proper oil distribution. The oil splashing due to gear rotation is also captured in the simulation. The quasi-steady state and transient evolution temperature field of the motor is predicted with the conditions as considered in the experimental setup. The predicted temperature of the windings is compared with experiment measurements at 29 different locations and the comparison is good.
